title.zh: 卷一百九十五 列傳第一百四十五: 迴紇
title.raw: 卷一百九十五 列傳第一百四十五: 迴紇 Volume 195 Biographies 145: Huihu

sentences.zh: 初，有特健俟斤死，有子曰菩薩，部落以為賢而立之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Tekin irkin died, he had a son named Pusa; the tribes considered him worthy and installed him as leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, when the chieftain Tekin irkin died, he left a son named Pusa. The tribes judged him capable and raised him to lead them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，菩薩與薛延陀侵突厥北邊，突厥頡利可汗遣子欲谷設率十萬騎討之。

translations.literal: At the start of the Zhenguan reign, Pusa and the Xueyantuo raided the northern marches of the Turks; the Turkish qaghan Jieli sent his son Yugu she at the head of a hundred thousand horsemen to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, Pusa joined the Xueyantuo in raiding the Turks' northern frontier. Qaghan Jieli of the Turks dispatched his son Yugu she with a hundred thousand cavalry to chastise them.

sentences.zh: 菩薩領騎五千與戰，破之於馬鬣山。

translations.literal: Pusa led five thousand horsemen into battle and defeated them at Mount Mane.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa led five thousand horsemen to meet them and broke their force at Mount Mane.

sentences.zh: 因逐北至於天山，又進擊，大破之，俘其部眾，回紇由是大振。

translations.literal: He pursued them northward to the Heavenly Mountains, attacked again, and inflicted a great defeat, capturing many of their tribesmen; thereby the Huihe rose greatly in power.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing north to the Heavenly Mountains, he struck again and shattered them, taking many captives. From that victory the Huihe gained tremendous momentum.

sentences.zh: 因率其眾附於薛延陀，號菩薩為「活頡利發」，仍遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He then led his people to submit to the Xueyantuo; they styled Pusa "Huojielifa" and still sent envoys to offer tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought his people under the Xueyantuo, who titled Pusa Huojielifa and continued to send tribute missions to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 菩薩勁勇，有膽氣，善籌策，每對敵臨陣，必身先士卒，以少制眾，常以戰陣射獵為務。

translations.literal: Pusa was fierce and brave, bold in spirit and skilled in planning; whenever he faced the enemy in battle he always led from the front, defeating many with few, and constantly made war and the hunt his business.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa was fierce and resolute, bold in counsel. In every clash he rode at the fore, beating larger hosts with smaller bands, and lived for the hunt and the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 其母烏羅渾，主知爭訟之事，平反嚴明，部內齊肅。

translations.literal: His mother Wuluohun oversaw disputes and lawsuits; her judgments were strict and fair, and the tribe was orderly within.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Wuluohun presided over quarrels and lawsuits with stern, even-handed justice, and the tribe kept good order.

sentences.zh: 回紇之盛，由菩薩之興焉。

translations.literal: The greatness of the Huihe arose from the rise of Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe's ascent to greatness began with Pusa's rise.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，擒降突厥頡利等可汗之後，北虜唯菩薩、薛延陀為盛。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan period, after the capture and surrender of the Turkish qaghans such as Jieli, among the northern barbarians only Pusa and the Xueyantuo remained powerful.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, once qaghans like Jieli of the Turks had been taken and subdued, only Pusa and the Xueyantuo still held real power among the northern peoples.

sentences.zh: 太宗冊北突厥莫賀咄為可汗，遣統回紇、仆骨、同羅、思結、阿跌等部，回紇酋帥吐迷度與諸部大破薛延陀多彌可汗，遂並其部曲，奄有其地。

translations.literal: Taizong enfeoffed Moheduo of the Northern Turks as qaghan and had him command the Huihe, Pugu, Tongluo, Sijie, A-die, and other tribes; the Huihe chieftain Tumidu together with the other tribes thoroughly defeated Qaghan Duomi of the Xueyantuo, then absorbed their followers and suddenly held their lands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong invested Moheduo of the Northern Turks as qaghan and set him over the Huihe, Pugu, Tongluo, Sijie, A-die, and other tribes. The Huihe leader Tumidu allied with them to crush Duomi, qaghan of the Xueyantuo, annexed his followers, and seized their territory.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，南過賀蘭山，臨黃河，遣使入貢，以破薛延陀功，賜宴內殿。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan they marched south past Helan Mountain to the Yellow River, sent envoys with tribute, and for their merit in defeating the Xueyantuo were granted a banquet in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 20 they moved south past Helan Mountain to the Yellow River and sent tribute. For their victory over the Xueyantuo the court feasted them within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸靈武，受其降款，因請回鶻已南置郵遞，通管北方。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited Lingwu he accepted their surrender and pledge; they then asked to establish postal relays south of the Huihe and to administer the northern regions.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received their submission at Lingwu. They petitioned to run courier stations south of the Huihe homelands and to help govern the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 太宗為置六府七州，府置都督，州置刺史，府州皆置長史、司馬已下官主之。

translations.literal: Taizong established six prefectures and seven districts; each prefecture had a commander-in-chief and each district a prefect, and both prefectures and districts were staffed with secretaries, marshals, and other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong created six fu and seven zhou: each fu had a dudu (area commander), each zhou a cishi (prefect), and both were given secretaries, marshals, and subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 以回紇部為瀚海府，拜其俟利發吐迷度為懷化大將軍，兼瀚海都督。

translations.literal: The Huihe tribe was made the Hanhai Fu; Tumidu, their irkin, was appointed General Who Cherishes Transformation and concurrently Dudu of Hanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe were organized as Hanhai Fu. Their irkin Tumidu was named General Who Cherishes Transformation and concurrently Dudu of Hanhai.

sentences.zh: 時吐迷度已自稱可汗，署官號皆如突厥故事。

translations.literal: By then Tumidu had already styled himself qaghan, and the titles of his officials all followed Turkish custom.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tumidu had already taken the title of qaghan, and his official ranks mirrored Turkish practice.

sentences.zh: 以多覽為燕然府，仆骨為金徽府，拔野古為幽陵府，同羅為龜林府，思結為盧山府，渾都為臯蘭州，斛薩為高闕州，阿跌為雞田州，契苾為榆溪州，跌結為雞鹿州，阿布思為歸林州，白為寘顏州。

translations.literal: Duolan was made Yanran Fu, Pugu Jinwei Fu, Bayegu Youling Fu, Tongluo Guilin Fu, Sijie Lushan Fu, Hundu Gaolan Zhou, Husa Gaoque Zhou, A-die Jitian Zhou, Qibi Yuxi Zhou, Diejie Jilu Zhou, Abusi Guilin Zhou, and Baixi Zhiyan Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duolan became Yanran Fu; Pugu, Jinwei Fu; Bayegu, Youling Fu; Tongluo, Guilin Fu; Sijie, Lushan Fu; Hundu, Gaolan Zhou; Husa, Gaoque Zhou; A-die, Jitian Zhou; Qibi, Yuxi Zhou; Diejie, Jilu Zhou; Abusi, Guilin Zhou; and the Baixi, Zhiyan Zhou.

sentences.zh: 又以回紇西北結骨為堅昆府，其北骨利幹為玄闕州，東北俱羅勃為燭龍州。

translations.literal: Northwest of the Huihe the Jiegu were made Jian Kun Fu; north of them the Guligan were Xuanque Zhou, and to the northeast the Juluobo were Zhulong Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of the Huihe the Jiegu were made Jian Kun Fu; to their north the Guligan became Xuanque Zhou; to the northeast the Juluobo became Zhulong Zhou.

sentences.zh: 於故單於臺置燕然都護府統之，以導賓貢。

translations.literal: On the old Chanyu Terrace the Yanran Area Protectorate was placed to oversee them and guide tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: At the former Chanyu Terrace the court set up the Yanran Protectorate to oversee them and channel their tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十二年，吐迷度為其侄烏紇所殺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan, Tumidu was killed by his nephew Wuhe.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 22 Tumidu was murdered by his nephew Wuhe.

sentences.zh: 初，烏紇蒸其叔母，遂與俱陸莫賀達幹俱羅勃潛謀殺吐迷度以歸車鼻。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wuhe had taken his uncle's wife in marriage; he then secretly plotted with Julu Morihedagan of the Juluobo to kill Tumidu and return to Chebi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhe had earlier married his uncle's widow. He then conspired with Julu Morihedagan of the Juluobo to assassinate Tumidu and go over to Chebi.

sentences.zh: 烏紇、俱羅勃，並車鼻之婿也，烏紇遂夜領騎十余劫吐迷度，殺之。

translations.literal: Wuhe and Juluobo were both sons-in-law of Chebi; Wuhe then led a little more than ten horsemen by night to seize Tumidu and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Both Wuhe and Juluobo were Chebi's sons-in-law. One night Wuhe led barely a dozen riders, seized Tumidu, and slew him.

sentences.zh: 燕然副都護元禮臣遣人紿烏紇云：「將奏而為都督，替吐迷度也。

translations.literal: Yuan Lichen, vice protector of Yanran, sent a man to deceive Wuhe, saying: "I will memorialize the throne to make you dudu in Tumidu's place.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lichen, vice protector of Yanran, sent someone to trick Wuhe: "I shall report to the throne and have you appointed dudu to replace Tumidu."

sentences.zh: 」烏紇輕騎至禮臣所，跪拜致謝；

translations.literal: Wuhe came lightly mounted to Lichen's camp, knelt and bowed in thanks;
translations.idiomatic: Wuhe rode in lightly to Lichen's camp, knelt, and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 禮臣擒而斬之以聞。

translations.literal: Lichen seized and beheaded him, then reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Lichen seized him, beheaded him, and reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 太宗恐回紇部落攜離，十月，遣兵部尚書崔敦禮往安撫之，仍以敦禮為金山道副將軍。

translations.literal: Taizong feared the Huihe tribes would split apart; in the tenth month he sent Minister of War Cui Dunli to reassure them, and also appointed Dunli vice general of the Jingshan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Huihe might fracture, in the tenth month Taizong sent Cui Dunli, Minister of War, to pacify them and named him vice general of the Jingshan circuit.

sentences.zh: 贈吐迷度左衛大將軍，賻物及衣服設祭甚厚。

translations.literal: Tumidu was posthumously given the title of General of the Left Guard; funerary goods and robes for the rites were lavished.
translations.idiomatic: Tumidu was posthumously honored as General of the Left Guard, with generous funerary gifts and vestments for the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 以吐迷度子前左屯衛大將軍翊、左郎將婆閏為左驍衛大將軍、大俟利發、使持節回紇部落諸軍事、瀚海都督。

translations.literal: Tumidu's sons, the former General of the Left Garrison Guard Yi and Left Langjiang Porun, were made Generals of the Left Xiaowei Guard, great irkin, commissioners bearing the staff for Huihe tribal military affairs, and Dudu of Hanhai.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yi, former General of the Left Garrison Guard, and Porun, Left Langjiang, were appointed Generals of the Left Xiaowei Guard, great irkin, commissioners with the staff over Huihe tribal forces, and Dudu of Hanhai.

sentences.zh: 後俱羅勃來朝，太宗留之不遣。

translations.literal: Later Juluobo came to court; Taizong detained him and would not let him return.
translations.idiomatic: Later Juluobo presented himself at court; Taizong kept him and refused to let him leave.

sentences.zh: 詔西突厥可汗阿史那賀魯統五啜、五俟斤二十余部，居多羅斯水南，去西州馬行十五日程。

translations.literal: An edict had the Western Turkish qaghan Ashina Helu command the five Zhu and more than twenty tribes of the five irkin, dwelling south of the Duoluosi River, fifteen days' ride from Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed the Western Turkish qaghan Ashina Helu over the five Zhu and more than twenty irkin tribes living south of the Duoluosi River, fifteen days' march west of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 回紇不肯西屬突厥。

translations.literal: The Huihe refused to submit to the Turks in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe would not accept western Turkish overlordship.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，回鶻遣兵隨蕭嗣業討高麗。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui the Huihe sent troops with Xiao Siye to campaign against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 6 the Huihe furnished troops to join Xiao Siye's campaign against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，婆閏死，妹比粟毒主領回鶻，與同羅、仆固犯邊。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era Porun died; his sister Bisudu took charge of the Huihe and, with the Tongluo and Pugu, raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo Porun died. His sister Bisudu led the Huihe and, with the Tongluo and Pugu, struck the frontier.

sentences.zh: 高宗命鄭仁泰討平仆固等，比粟毒敗走，因以鐵勒本部為天山縣。

translations.literal: Gaozong ordered Zheng Rentai to suppress the Pugu and others; Bisudu fled in defeat, and the Tiele heartland was made Tianshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong sent Zheng Rentai to crush the Pugu and their allies. Bisudu fled in defeat, and the Tiele homeland was organized as Tianshan County.

sentences.zh: 永隆中，獨解支，嗣聖中，伏帝匐。

translations.literal: In the Yonglong era, Dujiezhi; in the Sisheng era, Fudifu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yonglong, Dujiezhi ruled; under Sisheng, Fudifu.

sentences.zh: 開元中，承宗、伏帝難，並繼為酋長，皆受都督號，以統蕃州，左殺右殺分管諸部。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Chengzong and Funandu succeeded one another as chieftains, all bearing the title of dudu to govern Fanzhou, with left and right sha each administering subdivisions.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan, Chengzong and Funandu succeeded one another as chieftains, each holding a dudu title to govern Fanzhou, with left and right sha dividing the sub-tribes.

sentences.zh: 開元中，回鶻漸盛，殺涼州都督王君掞，斷安西諸國入長安路。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan the Huihe grew steadily stronger, killed Wang Juncuo, military governor of Liangzhou, and cut the road by which the states of Anxi reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan the Huihe waxed strong, slew Wang Juncuo, governor of Liangzhou, and severed the route from the Anxi protectorates to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 玄宗命郭知運等討逐，退保烏德健山，南去西城一千七百里。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Guo Zhiyun and others to pursue them; they withdrew to Mount Wudejian, seventeen hundred li south of the western city.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong sent Guo Zhiyun and others against them. They fell back to Mount Wudejian, seventeen hundred li south of the western stronghold.

sentences.zh: 西城即漢之高闕塞也。

translations.literal: The western city was the Han dynasty's Gaoque Pass.
translations.idiomatic: That western city stood where the Han had placed Gaoque Pass.

sentences.zh: 西城北去磧石口三百里。

translations.literal: North of the western city, three hundred li to Qishi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li north of the city lay Qishi Pass.

sentences.zh: 有十一都督，本九姓部落：一曰藥羅葛，即可汗之姓；

translations.literal: There were eleven dudu, originally from nine surname tribes: first, Yaoluoge, which was the qaghan's clan;
translations.idiomatic: They had eleven dudu drawn from nine "surname" tribes: first Yaoluoge, the qaghan's clan;

sentences.zh: 二曰胡咄葛；

translations.literal: second, Huduoge;
translations.idiomatic: second, Huduoge;

sentences.zh: 三曰咄羅勿；

translations.literal: third, Duoluowu;
translations.idiomatic: third, Duoluowu;

sentences.zh: 四曰貊歌息訖；

translations.literal: fourth, Mogexiqi;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, Mogexiqi;

sentences.zh: 五曰阿勿嘀；

translations.literal: fifth, Awudi;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, Awudi;

sentences.zh: 六曰葛薩；

translations.literal: sixth, Gesa;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, Gesa;

sentences.zh: 七曰斛嗢素；

translations.literal: seventh, Huwasu;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, Huwasu;

sentences.zh: 八曰藥勿葛；

translations.literal: eighth, Yaowuge;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, Yaowuge;

sentences.zh: 九曰奚耶勿。

translations.literal: ninth, Xiyawu.
translations.idiomatic: ninth, Xiyawu.

sentences.zh: 每一部落一都督。

translations.literal: Each tribe had one dudu.
translations.idiomatic: Each tribe had its own dudu.

sentences.zh: 破拔悉密，收一部落，破葛邏祿，收一部落，各置都督五人，統號十一部落。

translations.literal: Having defeated the Basmil and absorbed one tribe, and defeated the Karluk and absorbed another, they set up five dudu each and collectively called themselves the eleven tribes.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing the Basmil and annexing one tribe, then the Karluk and another, they appointed five dudu apiece and took the collective name of the eleven tribes.

sentences.zh: 每行止鬥戰，常以二客部落為軍鋒。

translations.literal: On every march or battle they regularly used two guest tribes as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On march or in battle they habitually placed two "guest" tribes at the army's point.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，其酋長葉護頡利吐發遣使入朝，封奉義王。

translations.literal: At the start of the Tianbao era their chieftain Yehu Telituofa sent envoys to court and was enfeoffed as Prince Who Upholds Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao their chief Yehu Telituofa sent envoys to court and was created Prince Who Upholds Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 三載，擊破拔悉密，自稱骨咄祿毗伽闕可汗。

translations.literal: In the third year they smashed the Basmil and styled themselves Qaghan Kutlug Bilge Köl.
translations.idiomatic: In year three they broke the Basmil and proclaimed Kutlug Bilge Köl Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 又遣使入朝，因冊為懷仁可汗。

translations.literal: They again sent envoys to court and were invested as Qaghan Who Cherishes Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys again and were invested as Qaghan Who Cherishes Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 及至德元載七月，肅宗於靈武即位。

translations.literal: By the seventh month of the first year of Zhide, Suzong had ascended the throne at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month of Zhide 1, Emperor Suzong had taken the throne at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 遣故邠王男承采，封為燉煌王，將軍石定番，使於回紇，以修好征兵。

translations.literal: He sent the former Prince of Bin, Nan Chengcai, enfeoffed as Prince of Dunhuang, and the general Shi Dingfan as envoys to the Huihe to renew friendship and request troops.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the former Prince of Bin, Nan Chengcai, now Prince of Dunhuang, and General Shi Dingfan to the Huihe to renew the alliance and ask for soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及至其牙，可汗以女嫁於承采，遣首領來朝，請和親，封回紇公主為毗伽公主。

translations.literal: When they reached the royal camp the qaghan gave his daughter in marriage to Chengcai; chieftains came to court seeking a marriage alliance, and the Huihe princess was titled Princess Piga.
translations.idiomatic: At the qaghan's camp the qaghan gave his daughter to Chengcai in marriage. Huihe leaders came to court to seal the alliance; the princess was titled Princess Piga.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在彭原，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Suzong was at Pengyuan and received them with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was at Pengyuan and treated them with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 二載二月，回紇又使首領大將軍多攬等十五人入朝。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year the Huihe again sent the great general Dolan and fifteen other chieftains to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year two the Huihe sent Great General Dolan and fifteen other leaders to court.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，加承采開府儀同三司，拜宗正卿，納回紇公主為妃。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the ninth month Chengcai was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of opening his own office, made Director of the Imperial Clan, and took the Huihe princess as consort.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the ninth month Chengcai was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with an open office, appointed Director of the Imperial Clan, and married the Huihe princess.

sentences.zh: 回紇遣其太子葉護領其將帝德等兵馬四千余眾，助國討逆。

translations.literal: The Huihe sent their crown prince Yehu leading generals Dide and others with a little more than four thousand soldiers to help the state suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe sent Crown Prince Yehu with Generals Dide and others and somewhat more than four thousand horsemen to aid the dynasty against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 肅宗宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Suzong feasted and rewarded them lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong feasted them and heaped rewards upon them.

sentences.zh: 又命元帥廣平王見葉護，約為兄弟，接之頗有恩義。

translations.literal: He also ordered the commander-in-chief, the Prince of Guangping, to meet Yehu and covenant as brothers; the reception was full of kindness and obligation.
translations.idiomatic: He had the commander-in-chief, the Prince of Guangping, receive Yehu and swear brotherhood; the welcome was warm with obligation and grace.

sentences.zh: 葉護大喜，謂王為兄。

translations.literal: Yehu was greatly pleased and addressed the prince as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu was delighted and called the prince "elder brother."

sentences.zh: 戊子，回紇大首領達幹等一十三人先至扶風，與朔方將士見僕射郭子儀。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi the great Huihe chieftains Dagan and twelve others arrived first at Fufeng and met the Puguoyi minister Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day thirteen great Huihe chiefs including Dagan reached Fufeng first and were received by Minister Guo Ziyi of the Puguoyi faction.

sentences.zh: 留之，宴設三日。

translations.literal: He detained them and feasted them for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Guo detained them and held feasts for three days.

sentences.zh: 葉護太子曰：「國家有難，遠來相助，何暇食為！

translations.literal: The crown prince Yehu said: "The state is in peril and we have come from afar to help—how can we linger over food!
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yehu said: "The empire is in crisis and we rode far to help—what time is there for feasting!

sentences.zh: 」子儀固留之，宴畢便發。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi insisted they stay; when the banquet ended they set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi pressed them to stay, but as soon as the banquet ended they marched.

sentences.zh: 其軍每日給羊二百口、牛二十頭、米四十碩。

translations.literal: Each day their army was supplied two hundred sheep, twenty cattle, and forty shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Daily their force was rationed two hundred sheep, twenty oxen, and forty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 及元帥廣平王率郭子儀等至香積寺東二十里，西臨澧水。

translations.literal: When the commander-in-chief the Prince of Guangping led Guo Ziyi and others to a point twenty li east of Xiangji Temple, they faced the Li River on the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping, commander-in-chief, led Guo Ziyi and the host to a camp twenty li east of Xiangji Temple, with the Li River at their west.

sentences.zh: 賊埋精騎於大營東，將襲我軍之背。

translations.literal: The rebels had hidden elite cavalry east of the great camp, intending to strike our army from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel elite cavalry lay concealed east of the main camp, poised to hit the Tang force in the rear.

sentences.zh: 朔方左廂兵馬使仆固懷恩指回紇馳救之，匹馬不歸，因收西京。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en of the Puguoyi left wing pointed the Huihe to gallop to the rescue; not a horse returned, and thereby the Western Capital was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en of the Puguoyi left wing sent the Huihe charging to the rescue. Not one horse came back from that ride—and with it they retook the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，廣平王、副元帥郭子儀領回紇兵馬，與賊戰於陜西。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Prince of Guangping and vice commander-in-chief Guo Ziyi led Huihe horsemen and fought the rebels at Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Prince of Guangping and vice commander Guo Ziyi led Huihe cavalry against the rebels at Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 初，次於曲沃，葉護使其將軍車鼻施吐撥裴羅等旁南山而東，遇賊伏兵於谷中，盡殪之。

translations.literal: At first they halted at Quwo; Yehu had his generals Chenbi Shitupo Peiluo and others skirt the southern mountains eastward and annihilated rebel ambushers in the valley.
translations.idiomatic: They first encamped at Quwo. Yehu sent Generals Chenbi, Shitupo, Peiluo, and others along the southern hills eastward and wiped out rebel ambushers in the ravines.

sentences.zh: 子儀至新店，遇賊戰，軍卻數里。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi reached Xindian and engaged the rebels, the army fell back several li.
translations.idiomatic: At Xindian Guo Ziyi met the rebels in battle and the line gave ground several li.

sentences.zh: 回紇望見，逾山西嶺上曳白旗而趨擊之，直出其後，賊眾大敗，軍而北坑，逐北二十餘里，人馬相枕藉，蹂踐而死者不可勝數，斬首十余萬，伏屍三十里。

translations.literal: The Huihe saw this, crossed the mountain's western ridge with white banners streaming, and charged straight at the enemy rear; the rebel host was utterly broken. Corpses filled the northern ditch as they pursued twenty-odd li—men and horses piled atop one another, trampled to death beyond counting; heads severed numbered more than a hundred thousand, and the slain lay thick for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe saw it, surged over the western ridge with white banners flying, and struck the enemy from behind. The rebel army collapsed. Bodies choked the northern ditch as pursuit ran twenty li and more—men and horses heaped and trampled beyond reckoning; more than a hundred thousand heads were taken, and the dead carpeted the ground for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 賊黨嚴莊馳告安慶緒，率其黨背東京北走渡河，而葉護從廣平王、僕射郭子儀入東京。

translations.literal: The rebel Yan Zhuang galloped to warn An Qingxu; he led his faction north out of the Eastern Capital, crossed the river in flight, while Yehu followed the Prince of Guangping and Minister Guo Ziyi into the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Yan Zhuang raced to warn An Qingxu, who fled north from the Eastern Capital across the river. Yehu entered the Eastern Capital with the Prince of Guangping and Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 初，收西京，回紇欲入城劫掠，廣平王固止之。

translations.literal: When the Western Capital was first taken, the Huihe wished to enter the city to plunder; the Prince of Guangping firmly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Capital fell, the Huihe wanted to sack the city; the Prince of Guangping firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 及收東京，回紇遂入府庫收財帛，於市井村坊剽掠三日而止。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was taken, the Huihe entered the treasuries to gather silks and goods, and plundered markets and villages for three days before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital they looted the treasuries and markets and villages for three days before they ceased.

sentences.zh: 財物不可勝計，廣平王又賫之以錦罽寶貝，葉護大喜。

translations.literal: The goods were beyond reckoning; the Prince of Guangping again bestowed brocades, felts, and jewels, and Yehu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth beyond measure changed hands; the Prince of Guangping added brocades, felts, and gems, and Yehu rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 及肅宗還西京，十一月癸酉，葉護自東京至。

translations.literal: When Suzong returned to the Western Capital, on the day guiyou of the eleventh month Yehu arrived from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong came back to the Western Capital, on guiyou day in the eleventh month Yehu arrived from the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 敕百官於長樂驛迎，上御宣政殿宴勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the officials to welcome him at Changle Post Station and personally feasted and rewarded him in the Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent officials to welcome him at Changle Post; the emperor himself feasted and honored him in Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 葉護升殿，其余酋長列於階下，賜錦繡繒彩金銀器皿。

translations.literal: Yehu ascended the hall; the other chieftains stood on the steps below, and brocades, silks, gold, and silver vessels were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu mounted the hall while the other chiefs lined the steps below, receiving brocades, silks, gold, and silver ware.

sentences.zh: 及辭歸蕃，上謂曰：「能為國家就大事成義勇者，卿等力也。

translations.literal: When they took leave to return to their lands the emperor said: "You who have done great deeds for the state with courage and righteousness—it is your strength that accomplished this.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to return the emperor said: "Those who by courage and loyalty have served the state's great cause—you have borne the weight of it.

sentences.zh: 」葉護奏曰：「回紇戰兵，留在沙苑，今且須歸靈夏取馬，更收范陽，討除殘賊。

translations.literal: Yehu memorialized: "The Huihe battle troops remain at Shayuan; we must now return to Lingxia to fetch horses, then gather at Fanyang and exterminate the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu replied: "Our warriors still camp at Shayuan. We must ride back to Lingxia for horses, then rally at Fanyang to finish the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」己丑，詔曰：「功濟艱難，義存邦國，萬里絕域，一德同心，求之古今，所未聞也。

translations.literal: On the day jichou an edict said: "Merit that crosses hardship, righteousness that preserves the realm—ten thousand li beyond the borderlands, one virtue, one heart—sought through past and present, never before heard.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day an edict declared: "Merit through hardship, loyalty to the realm—unity of heart across ten thousand li of wilderness—such a thing is unheard of in all annals.

sentences.zh: 回紇葉護，特稟英姿，挺生奇略，言必忠信，行表溫良，才為萬人之敵，位列諸蕃之長。

translations.literal: Yehu of the Huihe was specially endowed with heroic bearing and born of singular strategy; his words were ever faithful, his conduct gentle and upright; his talent matched ten thousand men, and his rank stood first among the foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu of the Huihe bore heroic grace and rare stratagem; his word was trust, his manner warm and just; one man worth ten thousand, first among the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 屬匈醜亂常，中原未靖，以可汗有兄弟之約，與國家興父子之軍，奮其智謀，討彼兇逆，一鼓作氣，萬里摧鋒，二旬之間，兩京克定。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu villain disturbed order and the central plains were not yet tranquil, because the qaghan had a covenant of brotherhood he raised for the state an army like that between father and son; he exerted his wit and scheme to punish the violent rebels; with one drumbeat of spirit he shattered the foe ten thousand li away; within twenty days both capitals were secured.
translations.idiomatic: While the northern foe threw the realm into chaos and the heartland still trembled, the qaghan, bound by brotherhood, fielded for the dynasty an army with a father's and son's devotion. With one rush of spirit he broke the enemy a thousand leagues away; within twenty days both capitals stood restored.

sentences.zh: 力拔山嶽，精貫風雲，蒙犯不以辭其勞，急難無以逾其分。

translations.literal: His strength could uproot mountains, his spirit pierced the clouds; he braved hardship without pleading fatigue, and in urgent peril none exceeded his share of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Strength to move mountains, spirit to thread the clouds—he faced hardship without complaint and in crisis gave more than duty asked.

sentences.zh: 固可懸之日月，傳之子孫，豈惟裂土之封，誓河之賞而已矣！

translations.literal: Truly this may be hung beside sun and moon and passed to sons and grandsons; how could it be only the reward of a fief or an oath sworn by the river!
translations.idiomatic: Let this be set beside sun and moon and handed to sons and grandsons—not merely a fief or a covenant sworn by the Yellow River!

sentences.zh: 夫位之崇者，司空第一；

translations.literal: Of lofty rank, the Minister of Works is first;
translations.idiomatic: Among exalted offices, Minister of Works ranks first;

sentences.zh: 名之大者，封王最高。

translations.literal: Of great names, prince is highest.
translations.idiomatic: among great titles, prince is highest.

sentences.zh: 可司空、仍封忠義王，每載送絹二萬匹至朔方軍，宜差使受領。」

translations.literal: He may be Minister of Works and still enfeoffed as Prince of Loyal Righteousness; each year twenty thousand bolts of silk shall be delivered to the Shuofang army, and envoys shall be appointed to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Minister of Works and Prince of Loyal Righteousness; each year twenty thousand bolts of silk shall reach the Shuofang army for designated envoys to receive."

sentences.zh: 乾元元年五月壬申朔，回紇使多亥阿波八十人，黑衣大食酋長閣之等六人並朝見，至閣門爭長，通事舍人乃分為左右，從東西門並入。

translations.literal: On the first day renshen of the fifth month of the first year of Qianyuan, eighty Huihe envoys led by Duohe Abo and six chiefs of the Black-Robed Arabs led by Gezhi came to audience; at the Gate of the Phoenix Tower they quarreled over precedence, and the relay secretary divided them left and right, entering by the eastern and western gates together.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, first day of the fifth month of Qianyuan 1, eighty Huihe envoys under Duohe Abo and six Black-Robed Arab chiefs under Gezhi attended court. At the Phoenix Gate they disputed precedence; the relay secretary split them east and west and admitted them through both gates.

sentences.zh: 六月戊戌，宴回紇使於紫宸殿前。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu of the sixth month the Huihe envoys were feasted before the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day in the sixth month the court feasted the Huihe envoys before Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁亥，詔以幼女封為寧國公主出降。

translations.literal: In the seventh month on the day dinghai an edict enfeoffed a young daughter as Princess Ningguo to be sent in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the seventh month an edict created a young imperial daughter Princess Ningguo to marry the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 其降蕃日，仍以堂弟漢中郡王瑀為特進、試太常卿、攝御史大夫，充冊命英武威遠毗伽可汗使；

translations.literal: On the day of her descent to the barbarians, the emperor's younger cousin Wang Yu of Hanzhong was made Special Grand Master, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Acting Censor-in-Chief, commissioner to invest the heroic and mighty far-reaching Piga Qaghan;
translations.idiomatic: On the day she went to the frontier, the emperor's cousin Wang Yu, Prince of Hanzhong, was made Special Grand Master, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Acting Censor-in-Chief, commissioner to invest the heroic Piga Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 以堂侄左司郎中巽為兵部郎中、攝御史中丞、鴻臚卿，副之，兼充寧國公主禮會使。

translations.literal: His cousin's son Zuo Si Langzhong Xun was made Langzhong of the Ministry of War, Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Grand Herald, as deputy, and also commissioner for Princess Ningguo's marriage rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's cousin's son Xun, Left Directorate Langzhong, became War Ministry Langzhong, Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Grand Herald as deputy and commissioner for the princess's marriage ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 特差重臣開府儀同三司、行尚書右僕射、冀國公裴冕送至界首。

translations.literal: A specially appointed great minister, Pei Mian, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with open office, Acting Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, Duke of Ji, escorted her to the border.
translations.idiomatic: The distinguished minister Pei Mian—Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with open office, Acting Right Vice Minister, Duke of Ji—was sent to escort her to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以冊立回紇英武威遠毗伽可汗，上御宣政殿，漢中王瑀受冊命。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, for the investiture of the heroic and mighty far-reaching Piga Qaghan of the Huihe, the emperor attended the Xuanzheng Hall and Wang Yu of Hanzhong received the patent of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day, to invest the Huihe heroic Piga Qaghan, the emperor presided in Xuanzheng Hall while Wang Yu of Hanzhong received the investiture patent.

sentences.zh: 甲午，肅宗送寧國公主至咸陽磁門驛，公主泣而言曰：「國家事重，死且無恨！

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Suzong escorted Princess Ningguo to Cimen Post Station at Xianyang; the princess wept and said: "State affairs weigh heavily—even death I shall not regret!
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day, Emperor Suzong escorted Princess Ningguo as far as Cimen Post Station at Xianyang. The princess wept and said, "The affairs of state weigh heavily; even death I shall not regret!"

sentences.zh: 」上流涕而還。

translations.literal: " The sovereign wept with flowing tears and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as he turned back.

sentences.zh: 及瑀至其牙帳，毗伽闕可汗衣赭黃袍，胡帽，坐於帳中榻上，儀衛甚盛，引瑀立於帳外，謂瑀曰：「王是天可汗何親？

translations.literal: When Yu reached their royal tent, Qaghan Pigla wore a reddish-yellow robe and a Hu cap, sitting on a couch within the tent; guards and insignia were very grand. He had Yu stand outside the tent and said to Yu: "What kin is the king to the Heaven Qaghan?
translations.idiomatic: When Yu reached the qaghan's camp, Qaghan Pigla wore a reddish-yellow robe and a foreign hat and sat on a couch within the tent amid splendid guards. He had Yu stand outside the tent and asked, "What kin is the king to the Heaven Qaghan of Tang?"

sentences.zh: 」瑀曰：「是唐天子堂弟。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "He is the Tang Son of Heaven's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "He is the Tang Son of Heaven's younger cousin."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「於王上立者為誰？

translations.literal: " He asked again: "Who is the one standing above the king?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Who is the one standing above the king?"

sentences.zh: 」瑀曰：「中使雷盧俊。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "The palace envoy Lei Lujun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The palace envoy Lei Lujun."

sentences.zh: 」可汗又報曰：「中使是奴，何得向郎君上立？

translations.literal: " The qaghan replied again: "A palace envoy is a slave—how can he stand above a lordling?
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan replied, "A palace envoy is a servant—how dare he stand above a lordling?"

sentences.zh: 」雷盧俊竦懼，跳身向下立定。

translations.literal: " Lei Lujun, startled and afraid, leapt his body downward and stood fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Lujun, startled with fear, leapt down to a lower position and stood there.

sentences.zh: 瑀不拜而立。

translations.literal: Yu did not bow but stood.
translations.idiomatic: Yu did not prostrate himself but stood upright.

sentences.zh: 可汗報曰：「兩國主君臣有禮，何得不拜？

translations.literal: The qaghan replied: "Between the rulers and ministers of two states there is ritual—why not bow?
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan said, "Between the rulers and ministers of two states there is proper ritual—why will you not bow?"

sentences.zh: 」瑀曰：「唐天子以可汗有功，故將女嫁與可汗結姻好，比者中國與外蕃親，皆宗室子女，名為公主。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "The Tang Son of Heaven, because the qaghan has merit, therefore gives his daughter to marry the qaghan and form a marriage alliance. Hitherto when China and outer barbarians allied by marriage, all were clan children titled princess.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The Tang Son of Heaven, because the qaghan has rendered great service, has given his daughter in marriage to the qaghan to cement an alliance. Hitherto when China allied with foreign states by marriage, the brides have been daughters of the imperial clan titled princesses."

sentences.zh: 今寧國公主，天子真女，又有才貌，萬里嫁與可汗。

translations.literal: Now Princess Ningguo is the Son of Heaven's true daughter, and moreover has talent and beauty, sent ten thousand li to marry the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Princess Ningguo is the Son of Heaven's own daughter, endowed besides with talent and beauty, sent ten thousand li to marry the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 可汗是唐家天子女婿，合有禮數。

translations.literal: The qaghan is son-in-law to the Tang house Son of Heaven and ought to have ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan is son-in-law to the Tang Son of Heaven and ought to observe the proper courtesies.

sentences.zh: 豈得坐於榻上受詔命耶！

translations.literal: How can he sit on a couch and receive an edict!
translations.idiomatic: How can he sit on a couch and receive an imperial edict!"

sentences.zh: 」可汗乃起奉詔，便受冊命。

translations.literal: The qaghan then rose, received the edict, and at once accepted the investiture patent.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan then rose, received the edict with due ceremony, and accepted the patent of investiture.

sentences.zh: 翼日，冊公主為可敦，蕃酋歡欣曰：「唐國天子貴重，將真女來。

translations.literal: The next day they invested the princess as khatun; the barbarian chieftains rejoiced, saying: "The Son of Heaven of Tang is august—he sends his true daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the princess was invested as khatun. The foreign chieftains rejoiced, saying, "The Son of Heaven of Tang is truly august—he has sent his real daughter."

sentences.zh: 」瑀所送國信繒彩衣服金銀器皿，可汗盡分與衙官、酋長等。

translations.literal: " The silks, garments, gold, silver, and vessels Yu sent as state credentials the qaghan entirely divided among yamen officers and chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: The silks, garments, gold, silver, and vessels Yu had brought as state gifts the qaghan divided entirely among his officers and chieftains.

sentences.zh: 及瑀回，可汗獻馬五百匹、貂裘、白赩。

translations.literal: When Yu returned, the qaghan presented five hundred horses, sable furs, and white felt.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu returned, the qaghan presented five hundred horses, sable furs, and white felt.

sentences.zh: 八月，回紇使王子骨啜特勒及宰相帝德等驍將三千人助國討逆。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Huihe sent Prince Guochuo tele, Chancellor Dide, and other fierce generals—three thousand men—to aid the state in suppressing rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Huihe sent the prince Guochuo tele, the chancellor Dide, and other fierce generals with three thousand men to aid the state in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉其遠至，賜宴，命隨朔方行營使仆固懷恩押之。

translations.literal: Suzong commended their coming from afar, bestowed a banquet, and ordered Shuofang field commissioner Pugu Huai'en to escort and command them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong commended their coming from afar, feasted them, and ordered Pugu Huai'en, commissioner of the Shuofang field headquarters, to take command of them.

sentences.zh: 九月甲申，回紇使大首領蓋將等謝公主下降，兼奏破堅昆五萬人，宴於紫宸殿，賜物有差。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the ninth month, Huihe envoys led by great chieftain Gaijiang thanked the princess's descent in marriage and also reported crushing fifty thousand Jiankun; a banquet in Zichen Hall; gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the ninth month, the Huihe envoys led by the great chieftain Gaijiang thanked the court for the princess's marriage and also reported crushing fifty thousand Jiankun warriors. A banquet was held in Zichen Hall and gifts were dispensed according to rank.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲午，回紇使三婦人，謝寧國公主之聘也，賜宴紫宸殿。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the twelfth month, three Huihe women envoys thanked the betrothal of Princess Ningguo; a banquet in Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the twelfth month, three Huihe women came as envoys to thank the court for betrothing Princess Ningguo. A banquet was held in Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，回紇骨啜特勒等率眾從郭子儀與九節度於相州城下戰，不利。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan, Guochuo tele of the Huihe and others led their masses to follow Guo Ziyi and the nine commissioners in battle below Xiang Prefecture city; it was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan, Guochuo tele of the Huihe and others led their forces to fight with Guo Ziyi and the nine military commissioners below Xiang Prefecture; the engagement went against them.

sentences.zh: 三月壬子，回紇王子骨啜特勒及宰相帝德等十五人自相州奔於西京，肅宗宴之於紫宸殿，賞物有差。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the third month, Huihe Prince Guochuo tele, Chancellor Dide, and fifteen others fled from Xiang Prefecture to the Western Capital; Suzong feasted them in Zichen Hall; rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the third month, the Huihe prince Guochuo tele, Chancellor Dide, and fifteen others fled from Xiang Prefecture to the Western Capital. Emperor Suzong feasted them in Zichen Hall and rewarded them according to rank.

sentences.zh: 其月庚寅，回紇特勒辭還行營，上宴之於紫宸殿，賜物有差。

translations.literal: That month on gengyin, the Huihe tele took leave to return to the field camp; the sovereign feasted them in Zichen Hall; gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: That same month on the gengyin day, the Huihe tele took leave to return to the field camp. The emperor feasted them in Zichen Hall and bestowed gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以回紇王子新除左羽林軍大將軍、員外置，骨啜特勒為銀青光祿大夫、鴻臚卿、員外置。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the newly appointed Huihe prince, Grand General of the Left Winged Forest Army by extraordinary appointment, Guochuo tele, was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of Honglu by extraordinary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day, the newly appointed Huihe prince, Grand General of the Left Winged Forest Army by extraordinary appointment, Guochuo tele, was given the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made Director of Honglu by extraordinary appointment.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，回紇毗伽闕可汗死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Huihe Qaghan Pigla died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Qaghan Pigla of the Huihe died.

sentences.zh: 長子葉護先被殺，乃立其少子登裏可汗，其妻為可敦。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yehu had first been killed; they then enthroned his youngest son as Qaghan Dengli; his wife became khatun.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yehu had already been killed, so they enthroned his youngest son as Qaghan Dengli; his wife became khatun.

sentences.zh: 六月丙午，以左金吾衛將軍李通為試鴻臚卿、攝御史中丞，充吊祭回紇使。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the sixth month, Left Gold Crow Guard General Li Tong was made provisional Director of Honglu and Acting Censor, serving as envoy to condole and mourn with the Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the sixth month, Left Gold Crow Guard General Li Tong was made provisional Director of Honglu and Acting Censor to serve as envoy to condole and mourn with the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 毗伽闕可汗初死，其牙官、都督等欲以寧國公主殉葬。

translations.literal: When Qaghan Pigla had just died, his yamen officers and dudu wished to have Princess Ningguo follow in burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Qaghan Pigla had just died, his yamen officers and dudu wished to have Princess Ningguo buried alive with him.

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「我中國法，婿死，即持喪，朝夕哭臨，三年行服。

translations.literal: The princess said: "By my China's law, when the son-in-law dies, one then observes mourning, weeping morning and evening, for three years wearing mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "By the law of my country, when one's husband dies one observes mourning, weeping morning and evening, and wears mourning garb for three years.

sentences.zh: 今回紇娶婦，須慕中國禮。

translations.literal: Now the Huihe have taken a wife—they must admire Chinese rites.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Huihe have taken a wife, they ought to emulate Chinese rites.

sentences.zh: 若今依本國法，何須萬里結婚。

translations.literal: If now they follow their native state's law, what need to seek marriage ten thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: If they follow their native customs now, what need was there to seek marriage ten thousand li away?"

sentences.zh: 」然公主亦依回紇法，剺面大哭，竟以無子得歸。

translations.literal: Yet the princess also followed Huihe law, scarifying her face and weeping greatly; in the end, because she had no son, she was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the princess also followed Huihe custom, slashing her face and weeping bitterly, and in the end, because she had borne no son, was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，寧國公主自回紇還，詔百官於明鳳門外迎之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Princess Ningguo returned from the Huihe; an edict ordered the hundred officials to welcome her outside Mingfeng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, Princess Ningguo returned from the Huihe. An edict ordered the officials to welcome her outside Mingfeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 上元元年九月己丑，回紇九姓可汗使大臣俱陸莫達幹等入朝奉表起居。

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the ninth month of the first year of Shangyuan, the Nine Surname Qaghan of the Huihe sent minister Julumodagan and others to enter court with a memorial inquiring after health.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the ninth month of the first year of Shangyuan, the envoy of the Nine Surname Qaghan of the Huihe, the minister Julumodagan and others, entered court with a memorial to inquire after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，回紇使二十人於延英殿通謁，賜物有差。

translations.literal: On yimao, twenty Huihe envoys presented themselves in audience in Yanying Hall; gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day, twenty Huihe envoys presented themselves in Yanying Hall; gifts were dispensed according to rank.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊辰，回紇使延支伽羅等十人於延英殿謁見，賜物有差。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the eleventh month, ten Huihe envoys led by Yanzhijialuo were received in audience in Yanying Hall; gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the eleventh month, ten Huihe envoys led by Yanzhijialuo were received in audience in Yanying Hall; gifts were dispensed according to rank.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，代宗初即位，以史朝義尚在河洛，遣中使劉清潭征兵於回紇，又修舊好。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, when Daizong had just ascended, because Shi Chaoyi still remained in He-Luo, he dispatched palace envoy Liu Qingtan to levy troops among the Huihe and renew the old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, when Emperor Daizong had just ascended the throne, because Shi Chaoyi still held the He-Luo region, he dispatched the palace envoy Liu Qingtan to levy troops among the Huihe and renew the old friendship.

sentences.zh: 其秋，清潭入回紇庭，回紇已為史朝義所誘，雲唐家天子頻有大喪，國亂無主，請發兵來收府庫。

translations.literal: That autumn, when Qingtan entered the Huihe court, the Huihe had already been enticed by Shi Chaoyi, who said the Tang house Son of Heaven had repeatedly had great bereavements, the state was chaotic and without a ruler, and urged sending troops to seize the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Qingtan entered the Huihe court, the Huihe had already been enticed by Shi Chaoyi, who said the Tang Son of Heaven had repeatedly suffered bereavements, the realm was in chaos and leaderless, and urged them to send troops south to seize the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 可汗乃領眾而南，已八月矣。

translations.literal: The qaghan then led the masses south—it was already the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan then led his people south—it was already the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 清潭賫敕書國信至，可汗曰：「我聞唐家已無主，何為更有敕書？

translations.literal: Qingtan, bearing the edict and state credentials, arrived; the qaghan said: "I have heard the Tang house has no ruler—why is there still an edict?
translations.idiomatic: When Qingtan arrived bearing the imperial edict and state credentials, the qaghan said, "I have heard that Tang has no ruler—why is there still an edict?"

sentences.zh: 」中使對曰：「我唐家天子雖棄萬國，嗣天子廣平王天生英武，往年與回紇葉護兵馬同收兩京，破安慶緒，與可汗有故。

translations.literal: " The palace envoy replied: "Though our Tang Son of Heaven has left the myriad realms, the succeeding Son of Heaven, the Prince of Guangping, was born heroic and martial; in years past he joined Huihe Yehu's troops and horses to recover the two capitals and defeat An Qingxu—he has old ties with the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy replied, "Though our Tang Son of Heaven has left the myriad realms, the succeeding Son of Heaven, the Prince of Guangping, was born heroic and martial. In years past he joined forces with Qaghan Yehu of the Huihe to recover the two capitals and defeat An Qingxu; he and the qaghan are old allies.

sentences.zh: 又每年與可汗繒絹數萬匹，可汗豈忘之耶？

translations.literal: Moreover every year tens of thousands of rolls of silk are given the qaghan—has the qaghan forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every year tens of thousands of rolls of silk are sent to the qaghan—has the qaghan forgotten?"

sentences.zh: 」然回紇業已發至三城北，見荒城無戍卒，州縣盡為空壘，有輕唐色，乃遣使北收單於兵馬倉糧，又大辱清潭。

translations.literal: Yet the Huihe had already marched to the Three Cities north; seeing desolate cities without garrison troops and prefectures and districts all empty forts, they showed contempt for Tang; they sent envoys north to gather Chanyu troops, horses, and granaries, and grossly insulted Qingtan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Huihe had already marched as far as the Three Cities north of the frontier. Seeing desolate walled posts without garrison troops and prefectures and districts all reduced to empty forts, they looked down on Tang. They sent envoys north to gather the Chanyu garrison's troops, horses, and grain stores, and grossly insulted Qingtan.

sentences.zh: 清潭發使來奏云：「回紇登裏可汗傾國自來，有眾十萬，羊馬不知其數。

translations.literal: Qingtan dispatched a messenger to report: "Huihe Qaghan Dengli has brought the whole nation south; they have one hundred thousand men; sheep and horses beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan dispatched a messenger to report: "Qaghan Dengli of the Huihe has come south with the full strength of his nation—one hundred thousand men and sheep and horses beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 」京師大駭。

translations.literal: " The capital was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was thrown into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 上使殿中監藥子昂馳勞之。

translations.literal: The sovereign sent Director of the Palace Administration Yao Zi'ang posthaste to greet and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Director of the Palace Administration Yao Zi'ang posthaste to greet and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 及於太原北忻州南，子昂密數其丁壯，得四千人，老小婦人相兼萬余人，戰馬四萬匹，牛羊不紀。

translations.literal: When south of Xin Prefecture, north of Taiyuan, Zi'ang secretly counted their fighting men and got four thousand; with aged, children, and women together more than ten thousand; war horses forty thousand; cattle and sheep beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached a point south of Xin Prefecture, north of Taiyuan, Zi'ang secretly counted their fighting men and found four thousand; with the aged, children, and women together, more than ten thousand; war horses forty thousand; cattle and sheep beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 先是，毗伽闕可汗請以子婚，肅宗以仆固懷恩女嫁之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qaghan Pigla had asked to marry by son; Suzong gave Pugu Huai'en's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qaghan Pigla had asked for a marriage alliance for his son, and Emperor Suzong gave him Pugu Huai'en's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及是為可敦，與可汗同來，請懷恩及懷恩母相見。

translations.literal: She now served as khatun and came with the qaghan, asking to meet Huai'en and Huai'en's mother.
translations.idiomatic: She now came as khatun together with the qaghan and asked to meet Huai'en and Huai'en's mother.

sentences.zh: 上敕懷恩自汾州見之於太原。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Huai'en from Fen Prefecture to meet them at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Huai'en to go from Fen Prefecture to meet them at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 懷恩又諫國家恩信不可違背。

translations.literal: Huai'en also admonished that the state's grace and trust must not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en also admonished that the state's grace and good faith must not be betrayed.

sentences.zh: 初欲自蒲關入，取沙苑路，由潼關東向破賊，子昂說之云：「國家頻遭寇逆，州縣虛乏，難為供擬，恐可汗失望，不如取土門路入，直取邢、洺、衛、懷。

translations.literal: They had first intended to enter from Puguan, take the Shayuan route, and break the rebels by advancing east from Tong Pass; Zi'ang urged: "The state has repeatedly suffered banditry; prefectures and districts are depleted and hard to supply—lest the qaghan be disappointed, better take the Tumen route and strike directly at Xing, Ming, Wei, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: They had initially intended to enter through Puguan Pass, take the Shayuan route, and break the rebels by advancing east from Tong Pass. Zi'ang urged them, saying, "The state has suffered repeated invasions; prefectures and districts are depleted and cannot easily supply your needs—lest the qaghan be disappointed, it would be better to take the Tumen route and strike directly at Xing, Ming, Wei, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 賊中兵馬盡在東京，可汗收其財帛，束裝南向，最為上策。

translations.literal: The rebels' troops and horses are all at the Eastern Capital; let the qaghan gather their wealth and baggage and march south—that is the finest stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' troops are all at the Eastern Capital; let the qaghan gather their wealth and baggage and march south—that is the finest stratagem."

sentences.zh: 」可汗不從。

translations.literal: The qaghan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 又說：「取懷州太行路，南據河陰之險，直扼賊之喉，亦上策也。

translations.literal: He urged again: "Take the Huai Prefecture Taihang route, hold south the strategic heights of Heyin, and seize the rebels' throat—that too is a superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang urged again: "Take the Taihang route through Huai Prefecture, hold the strategic heights south of the Yellow River, and seize the rebels by the throat—that too is a superior plan."

sentences.zh: 」可汗又不從。

translations.literal: The qaghan again did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Again the qaghan would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 又說：「取陜州太陽津路，食太原倉粟而東，與澤潞、河南、懷鄭節度同入，亦上策也。

translations.literal: He urged again: "Take the Shan Prefecture Taiyang Ford route, eat Taiyuan granary grain and march east, entering together with the Ze-Lu, Henan, and Huai-Zheng commissioners—that too is a superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: He urged once more: "Take the Taiyang Ford route through Shan Prefecture, eat grain from Taiyuan granaries and march east, entering together with the Ze-Lu, Henan, and Huai-Zheng commissioners—that too is a superior plan."

sentences.zh: 」可汗從之。

translations.literal: The qaghan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan agreed.

sentences.zh: 子昂因入奏，上以雍王適為兵馬元帥，加懷恩同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Zi'ang then entered to report; the sovereign made Prince Yong commander-in-chief and elevated Huai'en to co-minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang then entered to report, and the emperor appointed Prince Yong, Li Shi, commander-in-chief and elevated Huai'en to co-minister in the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 又以子昂兼御史中丞，與前潞府兼御史中丞魏琚為左右廂兵馬使，以中書舍人韋少華充元帥判官、兼掌書記，給事中李進兼御史中丞，充元帥行軍司馬，東會回紇。

translations.literal: He also made Zi'ang concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with former Ze-Lu concurrent Censor Wei Ju as left and right wing military commissioners; Secretariat Draftsman Wei Shaohua as commander adjutant and recorder; Imperial Diagnostician Li Jin concurrent Censor-in-Chief as army vice commander—they marched east to join the Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Zi'ang concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with the former Ze-Lu concurrent Censor Wei Ju as left and right wing military commissioners; Secretariat Draftsman Wei Shaohua served as the commander-in-chief's adjutant and recorder; Imperial Diagnostician Li Jin was concurrent Censor-in-Chief and army vice commander—they marched east to join the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 登裏可汗營於陜州黃河北。

translations.literal: Qaghan Dengli encamped north of the Yellow River in Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Dengli encamped north of the Yellow River in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元帥雍王領子昂等從而見之。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Prince Yong led Zi'ang and the others to follow and see him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Prince Yong led Zi'ang and the others to visit him.

sentences.zh: 可汗責雍王不於帳前舞蹈，禮倨。

translations.literal: The qaghan reproached Prince Yong for not dancing before the tent; his bearing was disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan reproached Prince Yong for not performing the dance of homage before the tent, calling his bearing disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 子昂辭以元帥是嫡孫，兩宮在殯，不合有舞蹈，回紇宰相及車鼻將軍庭詰曰：「唐天子與登裏可汗約為兄弟，今可汗即雍王叔，叔侄有禮數，何得不舞蹈？

translations.literal: Zi'ang pleaded that the commander-in-chief was the legitimate grandson and the two palaces were in mourning—inappropriate to dance; the Huihe chancellor and General Chenbi pressed in open court: "The Tang Son of Heaven and Qaghan Dengli are bound as brothers; the qaghan is Prince Yong's uncle—uncle and nephew have courtesies—why not dance?
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang pleaded that the commander-in-chief was the legitimate grandson and that with the two palaces still in mourning, dancing was improper. The Huihe chancellor and General Chenbi pressed him in open court: "The Tang Son of Heaven and Qaghan Dengli are bound as brothers; the qaghan is thus Prince Yong's uncle—uncle and nephew have their courtesies—why will he not dance?"

sentences.zh: 」子昂苦辭以身有喪禮，不合。

translations.literal: Zi'ang bitterly pleaded that personal mourning rites made it improper.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang protested bitterly that personal mourning rites made it improper.

sentences.zh: 又報云：「元帥即唐太子也，太子即儲君也，豈有中國儲君向外國可汗前舞蹈。

translations.literal: He also replied: "The commander-in-chief is the Tang heir apparent; the heir apparent is the stored lord—how could a Chinese stored lord dance before a foreign qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: He also replied, "The commander-in-chief is the Tang heir apparent; the heir apparent is the crown prince—how could a Chinese crown prince dance before a foreign qaghan?"

sentences.zh: 」相拒久之，車鼻遂引子昂、李進、少華、魏琚各搒捶一百，少華、琚因搒捶，一宿而死。

translations.literal: After a long standoff, Chenbi had Zi'ang, Li Jin, Shaohua, and Ju each beaten a hundred strokes with the rod; Shaohua and Ju died of the beating within one night.
translations.idiomatic: After a long standoff, Chenbi had Zi'ang, Li Jin, Shaohua, and Ju each beaten a hundred strokes with the rod. Shaohua and Ju died of the beating within a single night.

sentences.zh: 以王少年未諳事，放歸本營。

translations.literal: Because the prince was young and unfamiliar with affairs, he was released to return to his own camp.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prince was young and unfamiliar with affairs, he was released to return to his own camp.

sentences.zh: 而懷恩與回紇右殺為先鋒，及諸節度同攻賊，破之，史朝義率殘寇而走。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Huai'en and the Huihe yousha served as vanguard; together with the various commissioners they attacked the rebels, broke them, and Shi Chaoyi led the remnant band and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Huai'en and the Huihe yousha served as vanguard, and together with the various commissioners attacked the rebels, routed them, and Shi Chaoyi fled at the head of the remnant band.

sentences.zh: 元帥雍王退歸靈寶。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Prince Yong withdrew to Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Prince Yong withdrew to Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 回紇可汗繼進於河陽，列營而止數月。

translations.literal: The Huihe qaghan pressed on to Heyang, encamped, and halted for several months.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe qaghan pressed on to Heyang and encamped there for several months.

sentences.zh: 去營百餘里，人被剽劫逼辱，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: More than a hundred li from the camp, people were plundered, harassed, and humiliated beyond endurance.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred li from the camp, people were plundered, harassed, and humiliated beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 懷恩常為軍殿。

translations.literal: Huai'en habitually brought up the rear of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en habitually brought up the rear of the army.

sentences.zh: 及諸節度收河北州縣，仆固瑒與回紇之眾追躡二千餘里，至平州石城縣，梟朝義首而歸，河北悉平。

translations.literal: When the commissioners reconquered Hebei prefectures and districts, Pugu Yang with Huihe masses pursued more than two thousand li to Shicheng County in Ping Prefecture, took Shi Chaoyi's head and returned; all Hebei was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When the commissioners reconquered the prefectures and districts of Hebei, Pugu Yang pursued with Huihe forces for more than two thousand li to Shicheng County in Ping Prefecture, took Shi Chaoyi's head, and returned; all Hebei was pacified.

sentences.zh: 懷恩自相州西出崞口路而西，可汗自河陽北出澤、潞與懷恩會，歷太原。

translations.literal: Huai'en marched west from Xiang Prefecture through the Guokou route; the qaghan marched north from Heyang through Ze and Lu to join Huai'en, passing through Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en marched west from Xiang Prefecture through the Guokou route; the qaghan marched north from Heyang through Ze and Lu to join Huai'en, passing through Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遣使拔賀那上表賀收東京，並進逆賊史朝義旌旗等物。

translations.literal: They sent envoy Bahana to present a memorial congratulating the recovery of the Eastern Capital and to submit rebel Shi Chaoyi's banners and other items.
translations.idiomatic: They sent the envoy Bahana to present a memorial congratulating the recovery of the Eastern Capital and to submit rebel banners and other items of Shi Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 辭還蕃，代宗引見於內殿，賜彩二百段。

translations.literal: Taking leave to return to their realm, Daizong received them in the inner hall and gave two hundred rolls of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave to return to their realm, they were received by Daizong in the inner hall and given two hundred rolls of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 初，回紇至東京，以賊平，恣行殘忍，士女懼之，皆登聖善寺及白馬寺二閣以避之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Huihe reached the Eastern Capital, after the rebels were pacified they indulged in cruelty without restraint; men and women feared them and all climbed the two pagodas of Shengshan Temple and Baima Temple to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Huihe reached the Eastern Capital, after the rebels were crushed they indulged in savage cruelty without restraint. Men and women feared them and climbed the two pagodas of Shengshan Temple and Baima Temple to escape.

sentences.zh: 回紇縱火焚二閣，傷死者萬計，累旬火焰不止。

translations.literal: The Huihe set fire and burned both pagodas; dead and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands; for many tens of days the flames did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe set fire to both pagodas; the dead and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands, and the flames burned for many days without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 及是朝賀，又縱橫大辱官吏。

translations.literal: When they came to offer congratulations at court, they again ran riot, grossly humiliating officials.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to offer congratulations at court, they again ran riot, grossly humiliating officials.

sentences.zh: 以陜州節度使郭英乂權知東都留守。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Shan Prefecture Guo Yingyi was appointed acting eastern capital intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner of Shan Prefecture Guo Yingyi was appointed acting eastern capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 時東都再經賊亂，朔方軍及郭英乂、魚朝恩等軍不能禁暴，與回紇縱掠坊市及汝、鄭等州，比屋蕩盡，人悉以紙為衣，或有衣經者。

translations.literal: The eastern capital had twice passed through rebel chaos; the Shuofang army and the armies of Guo Yingyi and Yu Chao'en could not restrain violence; together with the Huihe they plundered wards and markets and Ru and Zheng prefectures until household after household was stripped bare; people all wore paper for clothing, or kasaya robes if they had any garment.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital had twice passed through rebel chaos, and the Shuofang army together with the forces of Guo Yingyi and Yu Chao'en could not restrain the violence. Together with the Huihe they plundered the wards and markets and the prefectures Ru and Zheng until household after household was stripped bare; people all wore paper for clothing, or saffron monks' robes if they possessed even that.

sentences.zh: 代宗禦宣政殿，出冊文，加冊可汗為登裏頡咄登密施含俱錄英義建功毗伽可汗，可敦加冊為婆墨光親麗華毗伽可敦。

translations.literal: Daizong took his seat in Xuangu Hall and issued the investiture document, further investing the qaghan as Qaghan Dengli Ketuo Dengmishi Hujulu Yingyi Jiangong Pigla, and investing the khatun as Khatun Pomo Guangqin Lihua Pigla.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong took his seat in Xuangu Hall and issued the investiture document, further investing the qaghan as Qaghan Dengli Ketuo Dengmishi Hujulu Yingyi Jiangong Pigla, and investing the khatun as Khatun Pomo Guangqin Lihua Pigla.

sentences.zh: 「頡咄」，華言「社稷法用」；

translations.literal: "Ketuo," in Chinese speech, means "state rites and implements";
translations.idiomatic: "Ketuo," in Chinese speech, means "rites and implements of state";

sentences.zh: 「登密施」，華言「封竟」；

translations.literal: "Dengmishi," in Chinese speech, means "investiture completed";
translations.idiomatic: "Dengmishi" means, in Chinese speech, "investiture completed";

sentences.zh: 「含俱錄」，華言「婁羅」；

translations.literal: "Hujulu," in Chinese speech, means "to gather and collect";
translations.idiomatic: "Hujulu" means, in Chinese speech, "to gather and collect";

sentences.zh: 「毗伽」，華言「足意智」。

translations.literal: "Pigla," in Chinese speech, means "sufficient in wisdom";
translations.idiomatic: "Pigla" means, in Chinese speech, "sufficient in wisdom";

sentences.zh: 「婆墨」，華言「得憐」。

translations.literal: "Pomo," in Chinese speech, means "worthy of compassion."
translations.idiomatic: "Pomo" means, in Chinese speech, "worthy of compassion."

sentences.zh: 以散騎常侍兼御史大夫王翊充使，就可汗行營行冊命焉。

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalry Regular Wang Yi, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was sent as envoy to perform investiture at the qaghan's field camp.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalry Regular Wang Yi, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was sent as envoy to perform the investiture at the qaghan's camp.

sentences.zh: 可汗、可敦及左右殺、諸都督、內外宰相已下，共加實封二千戶，令王翊就牙帳前禮冊。

translations.literal: The qaghan, khatun, left and right slash commanders, various dudu, and inner and outer chancellors and below were collectively granted two thousand additional allotted households; Wang Yi was to perform the investiture rite before the royal tent.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan, khatun, left and right slash commanders, various dudu, and inner and outer chancellors and all below were collectively granted two thousand additional allotted households in perpetuity, with Wang Yi performing the investiture rite before the royal tent.

sentences.zh: 左殺封為雄朔王，右殺封為寧朔王，胡祿都督封金河王，拔覽將軍封為靜漠王，諸都督一十一人並封國公。

translations.literal: The zuosha was enfeoffed as Prince Xiongshuo, the yousha as Prince Ningshuo, the Helu dudu as Prince Jinhe, General Balan as Prince Jingmo, and all eleven dudu as state dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The zuosha was enfeoffed as Prince Xiongshuo, the yousha as Prince Ningshuo, the dudu of the Helu as Prince Jinhe, General Balan as Prince Jingmo, and all eleven dudu were enfeoffed as state dukes.

sentences.zh: 尋而懷恩叛，投靈武，有朔方舊將任敷、張韶等，收合余燼，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Huai'en rebelled and fled to Lingwu; former Shuofang generals Ren Fu, Zhang Shao, and others gathered embers of defeat until their masses reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huai'en rebelled and fled to Lingwu. Former Shuofang generals Ren Fu, Zhang Shao, and others gathered the embers of defeat until their forces reached tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年秋，乃引吐蕃之眾數萬人至奉天縣，朔方節度郭子儀率眾拒之而退。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Guangde they led several tens of thousands of Tibetans to Fengtian County; Shuofang Military Commissioner Guo Ziyi led masses to resist and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Guangde they led several tens of thousands of Tibetans to Fengtian County. Shuofang Military Commissioner Guo Ziyi led troops to resist and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年秋，懷恩遣兵馬使範至誠、任敷將兵，又誘回紇、吐蕃、吐谷渾、党項、奴刺之眾二十余萬，以犯奉天、醴泉、鳳翔、同州等處，被其逆命。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Yongtai, Huai'en dispatched military commissioners Fan Zhicheng and Ren Fu at the head of troops, and enticed more than two hundred thousand of the Huihe, Tibetans, Tuyuhun, Tangut, and Nuci to attack Fengtian, Liquan, Fengxiang, Tong Prefecture, and other places in defiance of command.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Yongtai, Huai'en dispatched military commissioners Fan Zhicheng and Ren Fu at the head of troops, and enticed more than two hundred thousand men of the Huihe, Tibetans, Tuyuhun, Tangut, and Nuci to attack Fengtian, Liquan, Fengxiang, Tong Prefecture, and other places in defiance of imperial command.

sentences.zh: 先以郭子儀屯涇陽，渾日進屯奉天，數摧其鋒。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was first stationed at Jingyang and Hun Rijin at Fengtian, repeatedly blunting their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was first stationed at Jingyang and Hun Rijin at Fengtian, repeatedly blunting their advance.

sentences.zh: 又聞懷恩死，吐蕃將馬重英等十月初引退，取邠州舊路而歸。

translations.literal: When word came that Huai'en had died, Tibetan generals including Ma Chongying withdrew in the tenth month by the old road through Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Huai'en had died, the Tibetan generals including Ma Chongying withdrew in the tenth month by the old road through Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 回紇首領羅達幹等率其眾二千余騎，詣涇陽請降。

translations.literal: Huihe chieftain Luodagan and others led more than two thousand horsemen to Jingyang to offer surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe chieftain Luodagan and others led more than two thousand horsemen to Jingyang to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 子儀許之，率眾被甲持滿數千人。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi assented and led several thousand men in armor with bows drawn full.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi assented and led several thousand men in armor with bows drawn full.

sentences.zh: 回紇譯曰：「此來非惡心，要見令公。

translations.literal: The Huihe interpreter said: "We have come not with ill intent; we wish to see Lord Marshal."
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe interpreter said, "We did not come with hostile intent—we wish to see Lord Marshal."

sentences.zh: 」子儀曰：「我令公也。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi said: "I am Lord Marshal."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi said, "I am Lord Marshal."

sentences.zh: 」回紇曰：「請去甲。

translations.literal: The Huihe said: "Please remove your armor."
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe said, "Please lay aside your armor."

sentences.zh: 」子儀便脫兜鍪槍甲，策馬挺身而前。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi at once removed his helmet, spear, and armor, spurred his horse, and advanced alone.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi immediately doffed helmet, spear, and armor, spurred his horse forward, and rode out alone.

sentences.zh: 回紇酋長相顧曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The Huihe chieftains looked at one another and said: "It is he."
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe chieftains exchanged glances and said, "It is he."

sentences.zh: 」時太子太保李光進、兼御史大夫路嗣恭戎裝介馬在子儀之側。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Guangjin and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Lu Sigong, in full battle dress and mounted, were at Guo Ziyi's side.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Li Guangjin, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Lu Sigong, both in armor and mounted, flanked Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 子儀指視回紇曰：「此是渭北節度李太保。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi pointed toward the Huihe and said: "This is Li the Grand Protector, military governor of Weibei."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi gestured toward the Huihe and said, "This is Grand Protector Li, military governor of Weibei."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「此是朔方軍糧使路大夫。

translations.literal: He also said: "This is Minister Lu, grain commissioner of the Shuofang army."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "This is Minister Lu, grain commissioner of the Shuofang army."

sentences.zh: 」回紇便下馬羅拜，子儀亦下馬。

translations.literal: The Huihe at once dismounted and bowed in ranks; Guo Ziyi dismounted as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe immediately dismounted and bowed in formation; Guo Ziyi dismounted too.

sentences.zh: 回紇之眾為左右翼，各數百人，漸進；

translations.literal: The Huihe masses formed left and right wings, several hundred each, advancing gradually;
translations.idiomatic: Huihe warriors formed left and right wings of several hundred men each and advanced step by step;

sentences.zh: 子儀麾下亦馳而至，子儀麾退之。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi's subordinates also galloped up; Guo Ziyi waved them back.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's own troops galloped forward as well, but he gestured them to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 子儀命酒與之飲，贈之纏頭彩三千匹。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi ordered wine for them to drink and presented three thousand bolts of head-wrap silks as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi had wine brought for them and gave three thousand bolts of silk head-wraps as gifts.

sentences.zh: 子儀執回紇大將可汗弟合胡祿都督藥羅葛等手，責讓之曰：「我國家知汝回紇有功，報汝大厚，汝何背約負信，犯我王畿？

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi took the hand of the Huihe great general, the qaghan's younger brother Helu dudu Yaoluoge and others, and reproached them, saying: "Our state knew that you Huihe had merit and rewarded you most generously—why have you broken the covenant and betrayed trust, violating our royal domain?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi grasped the hand of the Huihe great general, the qaghan's younger brother Helu dudu Yaoluoge, and rebuked them: "Our empire knew your Huihe had rendered great service and lavished rewards upon you—why have you broken faith and invaded our capital region?

sentences.zh: 我須與汝戰，何乃降為！

translations.literal: If I must fight you, why have you come to surrender!
translations.idiomatic: If I were to fight you, why would you offer surrender?

sentences.zh: 我一身挺入汝營，任汝拘縶，我麾下將士，須與汝戰。

translations.literal: I alone have thrust myself into your camp; do as you will and seize me—but my officers and soldiers below will have to fight you."
translations.idiomatic: I have ridden alone into your camp; bind me if you wish—but my commanders and troops will surely fight you."

sentences.zh: 」回紇又譯曰：「懷恩負心，來報可汗，雲唐國天子今已向江淮，令公亦不主兵，我是以敢來。

translations.literal: The Huihe again interpreted: "Huai'en was faithless; he came to report to the qaghan, saying the Son of Heaven of Tang has now gone toward the Jiang-Huai, and Lord Marshal no longer commands troops—that is why we dared come.
translations.idiomatic: The interpreter spoke again for the Huihe: "Huai'en betrayed you; he told our qaghan that Tang's Son of Heaven had gone south to the Jiang-Huai and that Lord Marshal no longer held command—so we dared advance.

sentences.zh: 今知天可汗見在上郭，令公為將，懷恩天又殺之。

translations.literal: Now we know the Heaven Qaghan is still at Shangguo and Lord Marshal is the general, and Heaven has again killed Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Now we know the Heaven Qaghan remains at Shangguo and that you, Lord Marshal, command the army—and that Heaven has slain Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 今請追殺吐蕃，收其羊馬，以報國恩。

translations.literal: We now ask to pursue and kill the Tibetans and take their sheep and horses to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: We ask leave to pursue the Tibetans, seize their herds, and repay the empire's kindness.

sentences.zh: 然懷恩子，可敦兄弟，請勿殺之。

translations.literal: Yet Huai'en's sons, the khatun's brothers—please do not kill them."
translations.idiomatic: But Huai'en's sons, the khatun's brothers—spare them, we beg."

sentences.zh: 」合胡祿都督等與宰相磨咄莫賀達幹、宰相暾莫賀達幹、宰相護都毗伽將軍、宰相揭拉裴羅達幹、宰相梅錄大將軍羅達幹、平章事海盈闕達幹等，子儀先執杯，合胡祿都督請咒，子儀咒曰：「大唐天子萬萬歲！

translations.literal: Helu dudu and others, with chancellors Modu mohadagan, Tumo mohadagan, chancellor and Hudu pigla general, chancellor Jiela feiluodagan, chancellor and Meilu great general Luodagan, and Pingzhangshi Haiyingque dagan—Guo Ziyi first raised his cup; Helu dudu asked to swear an oath, and Guo Ziyi swore: "May the Son of Heaven of Great Tang live ten thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: Helu dudu, chancellors Modu mohadagan and Tumo mohadagan, the chancellor Hudu pigla general, chancellor Jiela feiluodagan, chancellor and Meilu great general Luodagan, and Pingzhangshi Haiyingque dagan were present. Guo Ziyi raised his cup first; Helu dudu requested an oath, and Guo Ziyi swore: "Long live the Son of Heaven of Great Tang!

sentences.zh: 回紇可汗亦萬歲！

translations.literal: Long live the Huihe qaghan as well!
translations.idiomatic: Long live the Huihe qaghan!

sentences.zh: 兩國將相亦萬歲！

translations.literal: Long live the generals and ministers of both states as well!
translations.idiomatic: Long live the generals and ministers of both realms!

sentences.zh: 若起負心違背盟約者，身死陣前，家口屠戮。

translations.literal: Whoever harbors a faithless heart and violates the covenant—may he die on the battlefield and his household be slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever turns faithless and breaks this pact—may he die in battle and his kin be put to the sword."

sentences.zh: 」合胡祿都督等失色，及杯至，即譯曰：「如令公盟約。

translations.literal: Helu dudu and the others turned pale; when the cup reached them, they at once interpreted: "As Lord Marshal's covenant."
translations.idiomatic: Helu dudu and the rest went pale; when the cup came to them, the interpreter said they accepted Lord Marshal's oath.

sentences.zh: 」皆喜曰：「初發本部來日，將巫師兩人來，云：『此行大安穩，然不與唐家兵馬鬥，見一大人即歸。
