translations.literal: All rejoiced and said: "On the day we set out from our headquarters we brought two shamans, who said: 'This journey will be very safe, yet you will not fight Tang troops—you will see a great man and return.'
translations.idiomatic: They all exclaimed in joy: "When we left our homeland we brought two shamans who said, 'This march will be wholly safe: you will not battle Tang forces—you will see a great man and turn back.'

sentences.zh: 』今日領兵見令公，令公不為疑，脫去衣甲，單騎相見，誰有此心膽！

translations.literal: Today leading troops we have seen Lord Marshal; Lord Marshal was not suspicious, removed robe and armor, and met us alone on horseback—who has such heart and gall!
translations.idiomatic: Today we came with an army and met Lord Marshal, who never doubted us, stripped off armor, and rode out alone to meet us—who else has such courage!

sentences.zh: 是不戰鬥見一大人，巫師有征矣！

translations.literal: Not to fight yet to see a great man—the shamans were prophetic!
translations.idiomatic: We did not fight yet we saw the great man—the shamans spoke true!

sentences.zh: 」歡躍久之。

translations.literal: They leapt and shouted for joy a long while.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted and danced for a long time.

sentences.zh: 子儀撫其背，首領等分纏頭彩以賞巫師，請諸將同擊吐蕃，子儀如其約。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi patted their backs; the chieftains divided the head-wrap silks to reward the shamans, asked the generals to join in attacking the Tibetans together, and Guo Ziyi kept the pact.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi clapped their shoulders; the chieftains shared the silks to reward the shamans, asked the Tang generals to strike the Tibetans with them, and Guo Ziyi honored the agreement.

sentences.zh: 翌日，使領回紇首領開府古野那等六人入京朝見。

translations.literal: The next day he sent Huihe chieftains including Kaifu Guyena and five others to enter the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent six Huihe chieftains, including Kaifu Guyena, to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 又五日，朔方先鋒兵馬使、開府、南陽郡王白元光與回紇兵馬合於涇州靈臺縣西五十里赤山嶺，共破吐蕃等十余萬眾，斬首五萬余級，生擒一萬余人，駝馬牛羊凡百里相繼，不可勝紀，收得蕃落五千余人。

translations.literal: Five days later, Shuofang vanguard military commissioner, Kaifu, Prince of Nanyang Bai Yuanguang joined Huihe forces at Chishan Ridge fifty li west of Lingtai County in Jing Prefecture; together they broke more than one hundred thousand Tibetans and others, beheaded more than fifty thousand, captured more than ten thousand alive; camels, horses, cattle, and sheep stretched for a hundred li without end—beyond counting—and more than five thousand Tibetan tribesmen were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Bai Yuanguang, Shuofang vanguard commissioner, Kaifu, and Prince of Nanyang, united with Huihe troops at Chishan Ridge fifty li west of Lingtai in Jingzhou and together shattered a Tibetan host of over one hundred thousand, taking more than fifty thousand heads and over ten thousand prisoners; camels, horses, cattle, and sheep lined the road for a hundred li without end, and more than five thousand Tibetan tribespeople were captured.

sentences.zh: 初白元光等到靈臺縣西，探知賊勢，為月明，思少陰晦，回紇使巫師便致風雪。

translations.literal: When Bai Yuanguang and the others first reached west of Lingtai County and reconnoitered the enemy, the moon was bright; wishing for more darkness, the Huihe had their shamans raise wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Yuanguang first reached the country west of Lingtai and scouted the enemy, the moon shone bright; wanting darker skies, the Huihe shamans summoned wind and snow.

sentences.zh: 及遲明戰，吐蕃盡寒凍，弓矢皆廢，披氈徐進，元光與回紇隨而殺之蔽野。

translations.literal: At dawn when battle was joined, the Tibetans were all frozen with cold; bows and arrows were useless; wrapped in felts they advanced slowly—Yuanguang and the Huihe followed and slew them until the field was hidden.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the Tibetans were numb with cold; bows and arrows failed them. Swathed in felts they crept forward; Yuanguang and the Huihe pressed after them and filled the plain with the slain.

sentences.zh: 仆固名臣，懷恩之侄，尤為驍將，亦領千余騎來降。

translations.literal: Pugu Mingchen, Huai'en's nephew and an especially fierce general, also led more than a thousand horsemen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Mingchen, Huai'en's nephew and a notably fierce commander, also came over with more than a thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋而子儀又使回紇宰相護地毗伽將軍，宰相梅錄大將軍、開府儀同三司、試太常卿羅達幹等一百九十六人來見。

translations.literal: Soon Guo Ziyi again had Huihe chancellor Hudi pigla general, chancellor and Meilu great general, Kaifu Yitong Sansi, provisional Taichang Qing Luodagan, and one hundred ninety-six others come for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guo Ziyi sent one hundred ninety-six Huihe dignitaries, including Chancellor Hudi pigla general and Chancellor Meilu great general Luodagan, Kaifu Yitong Sansi and provisional Taichang Qing, to present themselves.

sentences.zh: 上賜宴於延英殿，錫賫甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a banquet in Yanying Hall and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hosted them in Yanying Hall and lavished gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 閏月，子儀自涇陽領仆固名臣入奏，回紇進馬，及宴別，前後賫繒彩十萬匹而還。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Guo Ziyi led Pugu Mingchen from Jingyang to report at court; the Huihe presented horses, and at parting banquets before and after, they were sent back with one hundred thousand bolts of silk brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Guo Ziyi brought Pugu Mingchen from Jingyang to report at court. The Huihe offered horses, and after farewell banquets they departed with one hundred thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 時帑藏空虛，朝官無祿俸，隨月給手力，謂之資課錢。

translations.literal: At the time the treasury was empty; court officials had no salary stipends and received monthly "hand-strength" payments called zike money.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury stood empty; officials received no regular salaries but monthly hand-money called zike.

sentences.zh: 稅朝官閏十月、十一月、十二月課以供之。

translations.literal: A levy on officials' intercalary tenth, eleventh, and twelfth month dues was imposed to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: A levy on court officers' pay for the intercalary tenth, eleventh, and twelfth months was imposed to fund it.

sentences.zh: 大歷六年正月，回紇於鴻臚寺擅出坊市，掠人子女，所在官奪返，毆怒，以三百騎犯金光門、硃雀門。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dali, Huihe left Honglu Temple without permission into the wards and markets, seizing people's sons and daughters; local officials snatched them back, and in anger with three hundred horsemen they violated Jinguang Gate and Zhuque Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dali 6, Huihe burst from Honglu Temple into the city wards, abducting men and women. When officials recovered the captives, the Huihe in fury rode three hundred strong against Jinguang and Zhuque Gates.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇城諸門盡閉，上使中使劉清潭宣慰，乃止。

translations.literal: That day all gates of the Imperial City were shut; the emperor sent palace envoy Liu Qingtan to console them, and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That day every gate of the Imperial City was closed. The emperor sent palace envoy Liu Qingtan to reassure them, and they desisted.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，回紇出鴻臚寺，入坊市強暴，逐長安令邵說於含光門之街，奪說所乘馬將去。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year, Huihe left Honglu Temple, committed violence in the wards and markets, chased Chang'an magistrate Shao Yue down Hanguang Gate Street, and seized the horse Shuo was riding and took it away.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Dali 7, Huihe left Honglu Temple, rampaged through the markets, chased Chang'an magistrate Shao Yue along Hanguang Gate Street, and stole the horse he rode.

sentences.zh: 說脫身避走，有司不能禁。

translations.literal: Shuo slipped free and fled; the authorities could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo escaped on foot; the authorities were powerless to stop them.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，回紇一百四十人還蕃，以信物一千余乘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year, one hundred forty Huihe returned to their land with more than a thousand loads of gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Dali 8, one hundred forty Huihe departed for their homeland with more than a thousand loads of tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 回紇恃功，自乾元之後，屢遣使以馬和市繒帛，仍歲來市，以馬一匹易絹四十匹，動至數萬馬。

translations.literal: Relying on their merit, from the Qianyuan era onward the Huihe repeatedly sent envoys to trade horses for silk brocade; each year they came to market, one horse for forty bolts of silk, often reaching tens of thousands of horses.
translations.idiomatic: Counting on their services, from Qianyuan onward the Huihe sent envoys year after year to exchange horses for silk, one horse for forty bolts, often tens of thousands of animals at a time.

sentences.zh: 其使候遣繼留於鴻臚寺者非一，蕃得帛無厭，我得馬無用，朝廷甚苦之。

translations.literal: Their envoys awaiting dismissal stayed on at Honglu Temple—not a few—and the foreigners grew insatiable for silk while the horses we received were useless; the court suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys waiting to be sent home lingered at Honglu Temple in droves; the tribes never had enough silk while the horses Tang received were of little use, and the court was sorely burdened.

sentences.zh: 是時特詔厚賜遣之，示以廣恩，且俾知愧也。

translations.literal: At this time a special edict richly rewarded and dismissed them, showing broad grace and also that they might feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict now richly rewarded and dismissed them, displaying imperial generosity and hoping to stir their shame.

sentences.zh: 是月，回紇使使赤心領馬一萬匹來求市，代宗以馬價出於租賦，不欲重困於民，命有司量入計許市六千匹。

translations.literal: That month Huihe envoy Chixin led ten thousand horses to seek trade; Daizong, because horse prices came from land tax and did not wish to burden the people further, ordered the authorities to measure revenue and permit purchase of six thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: That month envoy Chixin brought ten thousand horses to sell. Daizong, unwilling to strain the people further since horse payments came from the land tax, ordered officials to reckon income and authorize purchase of six thousand.

sentences.zh: 十年九月，回紇白晝刺人於東市，市人執之，拘於萬年縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the tenth year, Huihe stabbed a man in broad daylight in the East Market; market people seized him and he was held in Wannian County jail.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Dali 10, Huihe killed a man in daylight at the East Market; townspeople seized him and he was jailed in Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 其首領赤心聞之，自鴻臚寺馳入縣獄，劫囚而出，斫傷獄吏。

translations.literal: When chieftain Chixin heard, he galloped from Honglu Temple into the county prison, broke out the prisoner, and hacked the jailers.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftain Chixin heard and raced from Honglu Temple into the county jail, freed the prisoner, and wounded the guards.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，回紇寇太原，過榆次、太谷，河東節度留後、太原尹、兼御史大夫鮑防與回紇戰於陽曲，我師敗績，死者千余人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, Huihe raided Taiyuan, passing through Yuci and Taigu; Hedong military governor and acting Taiyuan intendant Bao Fang fought the Huihe at Yangqu; our army was defeated and more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dali 13 the Huihe struck Taiyuan, marching through Yuci and Taigu. Bao Fang, acting Hedong governor and Taiyuan intendant, met them at Yangqu; Tang forces were routed and more than a thousand perished.

sentences.zh: 代州都督張光晟與回紇戰於羊武谷，破之，回紇引退。

translations.literal: Daizhou governor Zhang Guangsheng fought the Huihe at Yangwu Valley and defeated them; the Huihe withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Daizhou governor Zhang Guangsheng fought the Huihe at Yangwu Valley, defeated them, and they retreated.

sentences.zh: 先是，辛雲京守太原，回紇懼雲京，不敢窺並、代，知鮑防無武略，乃敢淩逼，賴光晟邀戰勝之，北人乃安。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xin Yunjing held Taiyuan, the Huihe feared Yunjing and did not dare look toward Bing and Dai; knowing Bao Fang lacked martial strategy, they dared press close—only when Guangsheng intercepted and won did northerners feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xin Yunjing held Taiyuan, the Huihe feared him and did not threaten Bing and Dai. Seeing Bao Fang as no soldier, they pressed in—only Zhang Guangsheng's victory restored calm in the north.

sentences.zh: 頓莫賀自立號為合骨咄祿毗伽可汗，使其酋長建達幹隨文秀來朝。

translations.literal: Dunmohe installed himself as qaghan with the title Heigudulu Pigla Qaghan and sent his chieftain Jiandagan to follow Wenxiu to court.
translations.idiomatic: Dunmohe proclaimed himself Qaghan Heigudulu Pigla and sent chieftain Jiandagan with Wenxiu to court.

sentences.zh: 命京兆尹源休持節冊為武義成功可汗。

translations.literal: Jingzhao intendant Yuan Xiu was ordered to bear credentials and invest him as Wuyi Chenggong Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu, Jingzhao intendant, was commissioned to invest him as Qaghan Wuyi Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年八月，回紇可汗遣首領墨啜達幹、多覽將軍合闕達幹等來貢方物，且請和親。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyuan, the Huihe qaghan sent chieftains including Mochuo dagan and Dolan general Hequedagan to present tribute and request a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhenyuan 3 the Huihe qaghan sent chieftains Mochuo dagan and Dolan general Hequedagan with tribute and a request for marriage.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，回紇公主及使至自蕃，德宗禦延喜門見之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, the Huihe princess and envoys arrived from their land; Dezong received them at Yanxi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhenyuan 4 the Huihe princess and envoys arrived; Dezong received them at Yanxi Gate.

sentences.zh: 時回紇可汗喜於和親，其禮甚恭，上言：「昔為兄弟，今為子婿，半子也。

translations.literal: The Huihe qaghan, delighted at the marriage, was very deferential in ritual and submitted: "Formerly we were brothers; now we are son-in-law—half a son."
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan, overjoyed at the alliance, was most respectful and wrote: "Once we were brothers; now I am your son-in-law—half a son."

sentences.zh: 」又詈辱吐蕃使者，及使大首領等妻妾凡五十六婦人來迎可敦，凡遣人千余，納聘馬二千。

translations.literal: He also reviled the Tibetan envoys; great chieftains sent wives totaling fifty-six women to welcome the khatun; more than a thousand people were dispatched, with two thousand betrothal horses.
translations.idiomatic: He insulted the Tibetan envoys as well. Great chieftains sent fifty-six wives to greet the khatun, over a thousand persons in all, and two thousand horses as bride-price.

sentences.zh: 德宗令朔州、太原分留七百人，其宰相首領皆至，分館鴻臚，將作。

translations.literal: Dezong ordered Shuozhou and Taiyuan each to retain seven hundred; their chancellor-chieftains all arrived and were quartered separately at Honglu and Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong ordered Shuozhou and Taiyuan each to host seven hundred men. Chancellor-chieftains all came and were lodged at Honglu and Jiangzuo.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，見於宣政殿。

translations.literal: On the day guisi they were received in Xuangu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi they were received in Xuangu Hall.

sentences.zh: 乙未，德宗召回紇公主出，使者對於麟德殿，各有頒賜。

translations.literal: On yiwei Dezong summoned the Huihe princess forth; envoys were answered at Linde Hall, each receiving distributions.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Dezong presented the Huihe princess; envoys were received at Linde Hall and each given gifts.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔鹹安公主降回紇可汗，仍置府官屬視親王例。

translations.literal: On gengzi an edict ordered Princess Xian'an to marry the Huihe qaghan, still establishing a princess's household on the model of an imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict wed Princess Xian'an to the Huihe qaghan and established a princess household like that of an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 以殿中監、嗣滕王湛然為鹹安公主婚禮使，關播檢校右僕射、送鹹安公主及冊回紇可汗使。

translations.literal: Palace Director and Heir of Teng Wang Zhanran was made marriage ritual commissioner; Guan Bo, acting Right Censor-in-Chief, was envoy to escort Princess Xian'an and invest the Huihe qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Director Zhanran, Heir of Teng, became marriage ritual commissioner; Guan Bo, acting Right Censor-in-Chief, escorted Princess Xian'an and invested the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年十二月，回紇汨咄祿長壽天親毗伽可汗薨，廢朝三日，文武三品已上就鴻臚寺吊其來使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Zhenyuan, Huihe Mizhulu Changshou Tianqin Pigla Qaghan died; court mourning was suspended three days, and civil and military officials of the third rank and above went to Honglu Temple to condole with the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhenyuan 5 Qaghan Mizhulu Changshou Tianqin Pigla died. Mourning halted court for three days; officials of third rank and above condoled the envoys at Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年六月，回紇使移職伽達幹歸蕃，賜馬價絹三十萬匹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Zhenyuan 6, Huihe envoy Yizhigedagan returned home; thirty thousand bolts of silk were granted as horse payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenyuan 6 envoy Yizhigedagan departed; thirty thousand bolts of silk were given as horse price.

sentences.zh: 以鴻臚卿郭鋒兼御史大夫，充冊回紇忠貞可汗使。

translations.literal: Honglu Qing Guo Feng, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was made envoy to invest the Huihe Zhongzhen Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Feng, Honglu Qing and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was appointed to invest Qaghan Zhongzhen.

sentences.zh: 是歲四月，忠貞可汗為其弟所殺而篡立。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month, Zhongzhen Qaghan was killed by his younger brother who usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fourth month Qaghan Zhongzhen was killed by his younger brother, who seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 時回紇大將頡幹迦斯西擊吐蕃未回，其次相率國人縱殺纂者而立忠貞之子為可汗，年方十六七。

translations.literal: The Huihe great general Yaganjiasi was campaigning west against Tibet and had not returned; the vice-chancellors led the people in killing the usurper and installed Zhongzhen's son as qaghan, only sixteen or seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Great general Yaganjiasi was still west fighting Tibet. Vice-chancellors led the nation to slay the usurper and raised Zhongzhen's son as qaghan, barely sixteen or seventeen.

sentences.zh: 及六月，頡幹迦斯西討回，將至牙帳，次相等懼其後有廢立，不欲漢使知之，留鋒數月而回。

translations.literal: By the sixth month Yaganjiasi returned from the western campaign nearing the royal tent; the vice-chancellors feared he would later depose and install rulers and did not wish Han envoys to know, detaining Feng for months before he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaganjiasi neared the royal camp in the sixth month, vice-chancellors fearing future depositions kept Han envoys ignorant and held Feng for months.

sentences.zh: 頡幹迦斯之至也，可汗等出迎郊野，陳郭鋒所送國信器幣，可汗與次將相等皆俯伏自說廢立之由，且請命曰：「惟大相生死之。

translations.literal: When Yaganjiasi arrived, the qaghan and others went out to welcome him in the suburbs, displaying the state gifts Guo Feng had brought; the qaghan and vice-generals all prostrated themselves explaining the deposition and installation, and requested orders: "Only the great chancellor decides life and death."
translations.idiomatic: Yaganjiasi's arrival brought the qaghan out to the suburbs with Guo Feng's gifts displayed. Qaghan and vice-generals prostrated themselves, explained the coup, and pleaded: "Only the great chancellor holds life and death."

sentences.zh: 」悉以所陳器幣贈頡幹迦斯以悅之。

translations.literal: They presented all the displayed vessels and silks to Yaganjiasi to please him.
translations.idiomatic: They gave Yaganjiasi all the displayed gifts to win his favor.

sentences.zh: 可汗又拜泣曰：「兒愚幼無知，今幸得立，惟仰食於阿爹。

translations.literal: The qaghan also bowed weeping and said: "The boy is foolish and young, now fortunate to be established—I rely only on eating from Father's hand."
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan bowed in tears: "Your son is young and ignorant; now that I am raised up, I live only by Father's bounty."

sentences.zh: 」可汗以子事之，頡幹迦斯以卑遜興感，乃相持號哭，遂執臣子之禮焉。

translations.literal: The qaghan treated him as a son; Yaganjiasi, moved by such humility, embraced him weeping, and they performed the rites of minister and son.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan addressed him as father; moved, Yaganjiasi wept in his arms and they observed lord-and-son rites.

sentences.zh: 盡以所陳器幣頒賜左右諸從行將士，己無所取，自是其國稍安，乃遣達比特勒梅錄將軍告忠貞可汗之哀於我，且請冊新君。

translations.literal: He distributed all presented gifts to accompanying officers and took nothing himself; thereafter the state grew somewhat settled, and they sent Tabitel Meilu general to announce Zhongzhen Qaghan's death to us and request investiture of the new ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He gave every gift to his officers and kept none. The realm calmed somewhat; they sent Tabitel Meilu general to announce Zhongzhen's death and seek investiture.

sentences.zh: 使至，廢朝三日，仍令三品已上官就鴻臚寺吊其使。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, court mourning was suspended three days; officials of third rank and above were again ordered to Honglu Temple to condole.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys arrived, court halted three days; officials third rank and above condoled at Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吐蕃陷北庭都護府。

translations.literal: That year Tibet captured Beiting Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tibet took Beiting Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 初，北庭、安西既假道於回紇以朝奏，因附庸焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Beiting and Anxi, having borrowed the Huihe road for memorials to court, became subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Beiting and Anxi had long used Huihe routes to reach court and thus fell under Huihe sway.

sentences.zh: 回紇征求無厭，北庭差近，凡生事之資，必強取之。

translations.literal: The Huihe demanded without end; Beiting being nearer, whatever resources for trouble-making they forcibly took.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe exacted endlessly; Beiting, being close, suffered forced seizures of every resource.

sentences.zh: 又有沙陀部落六千余帳，與北庭相依，亦屬於回紇，肆行抄奪，尤所厭苦。

translations.literal: The Shatuo tribe of more than six thousand tents, relying on Beiting and also subject to the Huihe, plundered freely and suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: More than six thousand Shatuo tents, tied to Beiting and subject to the Huihe, were plundered most bitterly.

sentences.zh: 其先葛祿部落及白服突厥素與回紇通和，亦憾其侵掠。

translations.literal: The Karluks and White-Dressed Turks had long been on good terms with the Huihe yet resented their raids.
translations.idiomatic: Karluks and White-Clad Turks, though allied with the Huihe, hated their predation.

sentences.zh: 因吐蕃厚賂見誘，遂附之。

translations.literal: Because Tibet richly bribed and enticed them, they attached themselves to it.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet's rich bribes drew them over.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃率葛祿、白服之眾去冬寇北庭，回紇大相頡幹迦斯率眾援之，頻敗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tibet led Karluk and White-Dressed forces the previous winter to raid Beiting; Huihe great chancellor Yaganjiasi led troops to aid them and was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet then led Karluks and White-Clad Turks against Beiting that winter; great chancellor Yaganjiasi marched to relieve them and lost repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃急攻之，北庭之人既苦回紇，乃舉城降焉，沙陀部落亦降。

translations.literal: Tibet pressed the attack fiercely; the people of Beiting, having suffered under the Huihe, surrendered the whole city, and the Shatuo tribe surrendered as well.
translations.idiomatic: Under fierce Tibetan assault, Beiting's people, weary of the Huihe, opened the city; the Shatuo submitted too.

sentences.zh: 節度使、檢校工部尚書楊襲古將麾下二千余眾出奔西州，頡幹利亦還。

translations.literal: Military governor and acting Minister of Works Yang Xigu led more than two thousand under his command to flee toward Xizhou; Yaganli also returned.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yang Xigu fled west toward Xizhou with two thousand men; Yaganli withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，悉其國丁壯五萬人，召襲古，將復焉。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year he mustered fifty thousand fighting men of the state, summoned Xigu, and intended to recover it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of Zhenyuan 10 he mobilized fifty thousand warriors and called Xigu to recover the protectorate.

sentences.zh: 俄為所敗，死者大半。

translations.literal: Soon they were defeated; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon beaten; more than half perished.

sentences.zh: 頡幹利收合余燼，晨夜奔還。

translations.literal: Yaganli gathered the embers and fled back day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yaganli gathered survivors and raced back night and day.

sentences.zh: 襲古余眾僅百六十，將復入西州，頡幹迦斯紿之曰：「第與我同至牙帳，當送君歸本朝。

translations.literal: Of Xigu's remnant barely one hundred sixty remained; as he was about to re-enter Xizhou, Yaganjiasi deceived him: "Just come with me to the royal tent and I will send you back to your court."
translations.idiomatic: Xigu had barely one hundred sixty left. As he sought Xizhou again, Yaganjiasi tricked him: "Come to the royal camp with me and I will send you home."

sentences.zh: 」既及牙帳，留而不遣，竟殺之。

translations.literal: When they reached the royal tent he detained him and would not release him, and in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the royal camp he detained and finally killed him.

sentences.zh: 自是安西阻絕，莫知存亡，唯西州之人，猶固守焉。

translations.literal: From this Anxi was cut off and none knew survival or death; only the people of Xizhou still held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi was severed from the empire; none knew who lived. Only Xizhou still held out.

sentences.zh: 頡士迦斯敗，葛祿乘勝取回紇之浮圖川，回紇震恐，悉遷西北部落羊馬於牙帳之南以避之。

translations.literal: After Yaganjiasi's defeat the Karluks seized Huihe's Futuchuan; the Huihe were terrified and moved all northwest tribes' sheep and horses south of the royal tent to escape.
translations.idiomatic: After Yaganjiasi's defeat Karluks took Futuchuan; terrified, the Huihe drove northwestern tribes' herds south of the royal camp.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年五月庚申朔，以鴻臚少卿庾鋌兼御史大夫，冊回紇可汗及吊祭使。

translations.literal: On the first day gengshen of the fifth month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan, Honglu Vice Minister Yu Duan, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was made envoy to invest the Huihe qaghan and perform condolence rites.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, first of the fifth month, Zhenyuan 7, Yu Duan, Honglu vice minister and Censor-in-Chief, was sent to invest the qaghan and mourn.

sentences.zh: 是月，回紇遣使律支達幹等來朝，告小寧國公主薨。

translations.literal: That month Huihe sent envoy Luzhidagan and others to court announcing the death of Princess Xiaoningguo.
translations.idiomatic: That month envoys including Luzhidagan announced Princess Xiaoningguo's death.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，故，肅宗以寧國公主降回紇，又以榮王女媵之；

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended three days; formerly, Suzong had married Princess Ningguo to the Huihe and sent a daughter of Prince Rong as her attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Court halted three days. Earlier Suzong had wed Princess Ningguo to the Huihe and sent Prince Rong's daughter as companion;

sentences.zh: 及寧國來歸，榮王女為可敦，回紇號為小寧國公主，歷配英武、英義二可汗。

translations.literal: when Ningguo returned, Prince Rong's daughter became khatun; the Huihe styled her Princess Xiaoningguo, successively married to Qaghans Yingwu and Yingyi.
translations.idiomatic: when Ningguo came home, Prince Rong's daughter became khatun, styled Princess Xiaoningguo, wife to Qaghans Yingwu and Yingyi.

sentences.zh: 及天親可汗立，出居於外，生英武二子，為天親可汗所殺。

translations.literal: When Tianqin Qaghan was established, she lived apart; she bore two sons to Yingwu, whom Tianqin Qaghan killed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqin Qaghan she lived apart; two sons by Yingwu were killed by Tianqin Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 無幾薨。

translations.literal: Before long she died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she died.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，回紇遣使獻敗吐蕃、葛祿於北庭所捷及其俘畜。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, Huihe sent envoys presenting spoils of defeating Tibet and the Karluks at Beiting and their captives and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhenyuan 7 Huihe envoys brought news of victory over Tibet and Karluks at Beiting with captives and herds.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃入靈州，為回紇所敗，夜以火攻，駭而退。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tibet entered Lingzhou it was defeated by the Huihe; at night they used fire attack and fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tibet had entered Lingzhou, been beaten by the Huihe, and fled in panic under a night fire assault.

sentences.zh: 十二月，回紇遣殺支將軍獻吐蕃俘大首領結心，德宗禦延喜門觀之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Huihe sent the killing-branch general presenting the great Tibetan captive chieftain Jiexin; Dezong viewed them at Yanxi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Huihe killing-branch general presented the great Tibetan captive chieftain Jiexin; Dezong watched from Yanxi Gate.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，以回紇藥羅葛靈檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, Huihe Yaoluoge Ling was made acting Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan 8 Yaoluoge Ling of the Huihe was appointed acting Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 靈本唐人，姓呂氏，因入回紇，為可汗養子，遂以可汗姓為藥羅葛靈，在國用事。

translations.literal: Ling was originally a Tang man, surname Lu; having entered the Huihe he became the qaghan's adopted son, and thus took the qaghan surname as Yaoluoge Ling and held power in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was born a Tang subject, family name Lu; entering Huihe service he became the qaghan's adopted son and took the royal surname Yaoluoge Ling, wielding power at court.

sentences.zh: 因來朝，寵賚甚厚，仍給市馬絹七萬匹。

translations.literal: Because he came to court, favors and gifts were very generous, and seventy thousand bolts of silk were still given for horse purchase.
translations.idiomatic: On this court visit he was showered with gifts, including seventy thousand bolts of silk for buying horses.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，遣使來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year, envoys came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhenyuan 9 envoys arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞元十一年六月庚寅，冊拜回紇騰裏邏羽錄沒密施合祿胡毗迦懷信可汗。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, sixth month, eleventh year of Zhenyuan, investiture was conferred making him Huihe Tengli Luoyulu Momishi Helu Hu Pigla Huaixin Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the sixth month of Zhenyuan 11 he was invested as Qaghan Tengli Luoyulu Momishi Helu Hu Pigla Huaixin.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，藹德曷裏祿沒弭施合密毗迦可汗遣使改為回鶻，義取回旋輕捷如鶻也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, Qaghan Aide Helilu Momishi Hemi Pigla changed the name to Huihu, taking the sense of wheeling light and swift as a hawk.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 4 Qaghan Aide Helilu Momishi Hemi Pigla renamed the people Huihu—"wheeling swift as a hawk."

sentences.zh: 八年四月，回鶻請和親，使伊難珠還蕃，宴於三殿，賜以銀器繒帛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Huihu requested marriage alliance; envoy Yinanzhu returned home and was banqueted in the Three Halls, given silver vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanhe 8 the Huihu sought marriage; envoy Yinanzhu was feasted in the Three Halls and given silver and silks on departure.

sentences.zh: 是歲，回鶻數千騎至䴙鵜泉，邊軍戒嚴。

translations.literal: That year several thousand Huihu horsemen reached Pipiquan; border troops stood on alert.
translations.idiomatic: That year several thousand Huihu riders reached Pipiquan; frontier garrisons went on alert.

sentences.zh: 十二月二日，宴歸國回鶻摩尼八人，令至中書見宰臣。

translations.literal: On the second day of the twelfth month, eight returning Huihu Manichaeans were banqueted and ordered to meet chancellors at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the second of the twelfth month eight returning Huihu Manichaeans were feasted and sent to meet chancellors at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是，回鶻請和親，憲宗使有司計之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huihu requested marriage alliance, Xianzong had the authorities calculate costs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Huihu asked to marry, Xianzong ordered officials to tally expenses.

sentences.zh: 禮費約五百萬貫，方內有誅討，未任其親，以摩尼為回鶻信奉，故使宰臣言其不可。

translations.literal: Ritual costs were about five million strings; within the realm punitive campaigns were underway and the marriage could not be undertaken; because the Manichaeans were revered among Huihu, chancellors were made to say it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies would cost some five million strings; campaigns still raged at home, so the match was deferred, and because the Huihu revered Mani, chancellors argued against the union.

sentences.zh: 乃詔宗正少卿李孝誠使於回鶻，太常博士殷侑副之，諭其來請之意。

translations.literal: An edict then sent Zongzheng Vice Director Li Xiaocheng as envoy to Huihu, Taichang Doctor Yin You as deputy, to explain the meaning of their request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Li Xiaocheng, vice director of the imperial clan office, to the Huihu with Taichang doctor Yin You as deputy to explain the court's response.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，毗迦保義可汗薨，輟朝三日，仍令諸司三品已上官就鴻臚寺吊其使者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, Qaghan Pigla Baoyi died; court mourning was suspended three days, and officials of third rank and above in all offices went to Honglu Temple to condole the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 1 Qaghan Pigla Baoyi died; court halted three days while officials third rank and above condoled envoys at Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 四月，正衙冊回鶻君長為登羅羽錄密施句主錄毗伽可汗，以少府監裴通為檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，持節冊立、兼吊祭使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, in the main court Huihu chieftains were invested as Qaghan Dengruoyulu Mishi Gouzhulu Pigla; Vice Minister of the Palace Store Pei Tong was made acting Left Regular Attendant and Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials to invest and mourn.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Huihu leader was invested as Qaghan Dengruoyulu Mishi Gouzhulu Pigla in the main audience hall; Pei Tong, vice minister of the palace store, was made acting Left Regular Attendant and Censor-in-Chief to invest and mourn.

sentences.zh: 五月，回鶻宰相、都督、公主、摩尼等五百七十三人入朝迎公主，於鴻臚寺安置。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Huihu chancellor, dudu, princess, Manichaeans, and five hundred seventy-three persons entered court to welcome the princess, lodged at Honglu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month five hundred seventy-three Huihu chancellors, dudu, princesses, and Manichaeans entered court to greet the princess and were lodged at Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 敕：「太和公主出降回鶻為可敦，宜令中書舍人王起赴鴻臚寺宣示；

translations.literal: Edict: "Princess Taihe is to marry down to the Huihu as khatun; Zhongshu Attendant Wang Qi should go to Honglu Temple to proclaim it;
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "Princess Taihe shall wed the Huihu qaghan as khatun; Zhongshu attendant Wang Qi shall proclaim this at Honglu Temple;

sentences.zh: 以左金吾衛大將軍胡證檢校戶部尚書，持節充送公主入回鶻及冊可汗使；

translations.literal: Left Jinwuwei Great General Hu Zheng, acting Minister of Revenue, bearing credentials as envoy to escort the princess into Huihu and invest the qaghan;
translations.idiomatic: Left Jinwuwei great general Hu Zheng, acting minister of revenue, shall escort the princess into Huihu and invest the qaghan;

sentences.zh: 光祿卿李憲加兼御史中丞，充副使；

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Banquets Li Xian additionally Censor Vice Director as deputy envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Director of imperial banquets Li Xian, additionally vice censor-in-chief, shall serve as deputy;

sentences.zh: 太常博士殷侑改殿中侍御史，充判官。

translations.literal: Taichang Doctor Yin You was changed to Palace Attendant Censor and made judge."
translations.idiomatic: Taichang doctor Yin You becomes palace attendant censor and judge."

sentences.zh: 」吐蕃犯青塞堡，以回紇和親故也。

translations.literal: Tibet attacked Qingsai Fort because of the Huihe marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet struck Qingsai Fort in reaction to the Huihu marriage.

sentences.zh: 鹽州刺史李文悅發兵擊退之。

translations.literal: Yanzhou governor Li Wenyue sent troops and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou governor Li Wenyue sent troops and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 回鶻奏：「以一萬騎出北庭，一萬騎出安西，拓吐蕃以迎太和公主歸國。

translations.literal: Huihu memorialized: "With ten thousand horsemen out of Beiting and ten thousand out of Anxi, we will expand against Tibet to welcome Princess Taihe home."
translations.idiomatic: The Huihu reported: "Ten thousand riders from Beiting and ten thousand from Anxi will press Tibet to escort Princess Taihe home."

sentences.zh: 」其月敕：「太和公主出降回紇，宜持置府，其官屬宜視親王例。」

translations.literal: That month edict: "Princess Taihe marries down to the Huihe; a household office should be established; its officials should follow the model of an imperial prince."
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict added: "Princess Taihe weds the Huihu; establish her household with officials on the model of an imperial prince."

sentences.zh: 回紇自鹹安公主歿後，屢歸款請繼前好，久未之許。

translations.literal: After Princess Xian'an died, the Huihe repeatedly sent pledges of goodwill seeking to renew the old bond, long denied.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Xian'an's death the Huihu repeatedly sued to renew the old tie, but permission was long withheld.

sentences.zh: 至元和末，其請彌切，憲宗以北虜有勛勞於王室，又西戎比歲為邊患，遂許以妻之。

translations.literal: By the end of Yuanhe their pleas grew urgent; Xianzong, because the northern barbarians had labored for the royal house and western Rong had yearly harassed the border, then consented to marry a princess to them.
translations.idiomatic: By late Yuanhe their pleas grew desperate; Xianzong, mindful of northern service to the throne and western raids, at last agreed to a princess.

sentences.zh: 既許而憲宗崩。

translations.literal: Once consent was given, Xianzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Consent had barely been given when Xianzong died.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，逾年乃封第十妹為太和公主，將出降，回紇登邏骨沒密施合毗伽可汗遣使伊難珠、句錄都督思結並外宰相、駙馬、梅錄司馬，兼公主一人、葉護公主一人，及達幹並駝馬千余來迎。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, more than a year passed before the tenth younger sister was enfeoffed as Princess Taihe; as she was to marry down, Huihu Qaghan Dengruogumu Mishi Hepigla sent envoys Yinanzhu, Judu dudu Sijie, outer chancellors, son-in-law, Meilu sima, with one princess, one Yehu princess, and dagan with more than a thousand camels and horses to welcome her.
translations.idiomatic: A year into Muzong's reign his tenth sister was made Princess Taihe. Qaghan Dengruogumu Mishi Hepigla sent Yinanzhu, Judu dudu Sijie, outer chancellors, a son-in-law, Meilu sima, a princess, a Yehu princess, and dagan with over a thousand camels and horses to meet her.

sentences.zh: 太和公主發赴回紇國，穆宗禦通化門左個臨送，使百僚章敬寺前立班，儀衛甚盛，士女傾城觀焉。

translations.literal: Princess Taihe set out for Huihu; Muzong attended at the left wing of Tonghua Gate to see her off, ordering the hundred officials to stand in formation before Zhangjing Temple—the guard was splendid and the city turned out to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe departed for the Huihu realm; Muzong saw her off at Tonghua Gate's left wing with officials lined before Zhangjing Temple in splendid array while the city watched.

sentences.zh: 十一月，振武節度張惟清奏：「準詔發兵三千赴蔚州，數內已發一千人訖，余二千人，待太和公主出界即發遣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhenwu governor Zhang Weiqing memorialized: "Per edict, three thousand troops are sent to Weizhou; within the quota one thousand have already been dispatched; the remaining two thousand will march once Princess Taihe crosses the border."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhenwu governor Zhang Weiqing reported: "Per edict three thousand men go to Weizhou; one thousand are already sent; the rest march when Princess Taihe leaves the border."

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「天德轉牒云：回鶻七百六十人將駝馬及車，相次至黃蘆泉迎候公主。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Tiande relay states seven hundred sixty Huihu with camels, horses, and carts are arriving in succession at Huangluquan to await the princess."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Tiande relays that seven hundred sixty Huihu with camels, horses, and carts are reaching Huangluquan in turn to greet her."

sentences.zh: 」豐州刺史李祐奏：「迎太和公主回鶻三千於卿泉下營拓吐蕃。」

translations.literal: Fengzhou governor Li You memorialized: "Three thousand Huihu welcoming Princess Taihe are encamped below Qingquan to expand against Tibet."
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhou governor Li You reported: "Three thousand Huihu escorts camp below Qingquan to press Tibet."

sentences.zh: 二年二月，賜回紇馬價絹五萬匹。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, five myriad bolts of silk were granted as Huihe horse payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2, fifty thousand bolts of silk were granted as horse price.

sentences.zh: 三月，又賜馬價絹七萬匹。

translations.literal: In the third month, another seventy thousand bolts of silk were granted as horse payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month another seventy thousand bolts followed as horse price.

sentences.zh: 是月，裴度招討幽、鎮之亂，回鶻請以兵從度討伐。

translations.literal: That month Pei Du was recruiting to suppress the You-Zhen rebellion; Huihu asked to follow Du with troops.
translations.idiomatic: That month Pei Du campaigned against the You-Zhen rebels; the Huihu offered troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 朝議以寶應初回紇收復兩京，恃功驕恣難制，鹹以為不可，遂命中使止回紇令歸。

translations.literal: Court discussion recalled how in the early Baoying era Huihe recovered the two capitals and, relying on merit, grew arrogant and hard to control—all deemed it impossible, and a palace envoy was ordered to stop the Huihu and send them home.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate recalled Baoying days when Huihe retook the capitals yet grew insolent with pride—all counseled refusal, and a palace envoy ordered them back.

sentences.zh: 會其已上豐州北界，不從。

translations.literal: They had already crossed north of Fengzhou and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: They had already passed Fengzhou's northern border and refused.

sentences.zh: 上詔發繒帛七萬匹賜之，方還。

translations.literal: An edict then sent seventy thousand bolts of silk as gift before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Only after an edict granted seventy thousand bolts of silk did they turn back.

sentences.zh: 五月，命使冊立登啰骨沒密施合毗伽禮可汗，遣品官田務豐領國信十二車使回鶻，賜可汗及太和公主。

translations.literal: In the fifth month envoys were ordered to invest Qaghan Dengruogumu Mishi Hepigla Li Qaghan; palace officer Tian Wufeng led twelve carts of state gifts to Huihu for the qaghan and Princess Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month envoys invested Qaghan Dengruogumu Mishi Hepigla Li; palace officer Tian Wufeng brought twelve carts of imperial gifts to the qaghan and Princess Taihe.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年閏十月，金吾大將軍胡證、副使光祿卿李憲、婚禮使衛尉卿李銳、副使宗正少卿李子鴻、判官虞部郎中張敏、太常博士殷侑送太和公主至自回紇，皆云：初，公主去回紇牙帳尚可信宿，可汗遣數百騎來請與公主先從他道去。

translations.literal: In the intercalary tenth month of Changqing year 2, Jinwu Great General Hu Zheng, deputy Li Xian, marriage ritual commissioner Weiwei Qing Li Rui, deputy Zongzheng Vice Director Li Zihong, judge Zhang Min of the Ministry of Works, Taichang Doctor Yin You escorted Princess Taihe back from Huihu—all said: at first when the princess left the Huihu royal tent it was still about one or two nights' journey; the qaghan sent several hundred horsemen asking the princess to go first by another road.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month of Changqing 2, Hu Zheng, Li Xian, Li Rui, Li Zihong, Zhang Min, and Yin You escorted Princess Taihe from the Huihu—all recounted: when she first left the royal camp the qaghan sent hundreds of riders asking her to take another road ahead.

sentences.zh: 胡證曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Hu Zheng said: "Impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zheng refused.

sentences.zh: 」虜使曰：「前鹹安公主來時，去花門數百里即先去，今何獨拒我？

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy said: "When Princess Xian'an came before, several hundred li from Huamen she went ahead—why refuse us alone now?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy protested: "When Princess Xian'an came she went ahead hundreds of li from Huamen—why block us?"

sentences.zh: 」證曰：「我天子詔送公主以投可汗，今未見可汗，豈宜先往！

translations.literal: Zheng said: "Our Son of Heaven's edict escorts the princess to the qaghan; having not yet seen the qaghan, how can she go ahead first!"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied: "The Son of Heaven commands us to deliver the princess to the qaghan; until he is seen, she cannot go ahead!"

sentences.zh: 」虜使乃止。

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy desisted.

sentences.zh: 既至虜庭，乃擇吉日，冊公主為回鶻可敦。

translations.literal: When they reached the barbarian court a lucky day was chosen and the princess was invested as Huihu khatun.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huihu court they chose an auspicious day to invest her as khatun.

sentences.zh: 可汗先升樓東向坐，設氈幄於樓下以居公主，使群胡主教公主以胡法。

translations.literal: The qaghan first ascended the tower facing east and sat; a felt pavilion was set below the tower for the princess, and groups of Hu elders were sent to teach the princess Hu ways.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan sat east-facing atop the tower; a felt pavilion below housed the princess while Hu elders taught her their customs.

sentences.zh: 公主始解唐服而衣胡服，以一嫗侍，出樓前西向拜。

translations.literal: The princess first removed Tang dress and wore Hu dress; one old woman attended as she came before the tower and bowed westward.
translations.idiomatic: She shed Tang robes for Hu garb; attended by an old woman she bowed west before the tower.

sentences.zh: 可汗坐而視，公主再俯拜訖，復入氈幄中，解前所服而披可敦服，通裾大襦，皆茜色，金飾冠如角，前指後出樓，俯拜可汗如初禮。

translations.literal: The qaghan sat watching; when the princess bowed twice she re-entered the felt pavilion, removed her former dress and donned khatun dress—full-skirted great robe, all madder red, gold crown like horns pointing fore and aft—and came out again bowing to the qaghan as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan watched as she bowed twice, returned to the pavilion, donned khatun robes of madder-red full skirts and a horned gold crown, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 虜先設大輿曲扆，前設小座，相者引公主升輿，回紇九姓相分負其輿，隨日右轉於庭者九，公主乃降輿升樓，與可汗俱東向坐。

translations.literal: The barbarians first set a great carriage with curved screens and a small seat before it; guides led the princess into the carriage; nine Huihu surnames bore it in turn, turning right nine times in the courtyard; the princess then descended, ascended the tower, and sat east with the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: They placed a great curtained carriage with a small seat; nine Huihu clans bore it, circling right nine times in the yard; she then mounted the tower and sat east with the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 自此臣下朝謁，並拜可敦。

translations.literal: From this ministers attending court all bowed to the khatun as well.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter courtiers bowed to the khatun as well.

sentences.zh: 可敦自有牙帳，命二相出入帳中。

translations.literal: The khatun had her own royal tent; two chancellors were ordered to enter and leave the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The khatun kept her own camp; two chancellors attended her tent.

sentences.zh: 證等將歸，可敦宴之帳中，留連號啼者竟日，可汗因贈漢使以厚貺。

translations.literal: When Zheng and the others were to return, the khatun banqueted them in the tent; weeping and wailing lasted the whole day; the qaghan therefore gave Han envoys rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: As Zheng's party prepared to leave, the khatun feasted them in her tent, weeping all day; the qaghan sent lavish parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，命中使以絹二十萬匹付鴻臚寺宣賜回鶻充馬價。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, a palace envoy was ordered to deliver two hundred thousand bolts of silk to Honglu Temple to bestow on Huihu as horse payment.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 a palace envoy delivered two hundred thousand bolts of silk through Honglu Temple as Huihu horse price.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，中使以絹二十三萬匹賜回紇充馬價。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, a palace envoy bestowed two hundred thirty thousand bolts of silk on Huihe as horse payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taihe 3 a palace envoy granted two hundred thirty thousand bolts to the Huihe as horse price.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，回紇李義節等將駝馬到，且報可汗三月二十七日薨，已冊親弟薩特勒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, Huihe Li Yijie and others brought camels and horses and reported the qaghan had died on the twenty-seventh day of the third month; his younger brother Sateler had been invested.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taihe 7 Li Yijie arrived with herds reporting the qaghan died on the twenty-seventh of the third month; younger brother Sateler was invested.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，仍令諸司文武三品、尚書省四品以上官就鴻臚寺吊其使者。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended three days; civil and military officials of third rank and above and Secretariat officials of fourth rank and above were ordered to Honglu Temple to condole the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Court halted three days; officials third rank and above and Secretariat fourth rank and above condoled at Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 以左驍衛將軍、皇城留守唐弘實為金吾將軍兼御史大夫，持節充入回鶻吊祭冊立使。

translations.literal: Left Xiaowei General and Imperial City Defender Tang Hongshi was made Jinwu General and Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials as envoy to enter Huihu to mourn, invest, and establish the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hongshi, left Xiaowei general and imperial city defender, was made Jinwu general and censor-in-chief to mourn, invest, and establish the new qaghan.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，入朝回鶻進太和公主所獻馬射女子七人，沙陀小兒二人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year, Huihu entering court presented seven women skilled in horseback archery given by Princess Taihe and two Shatuo boys.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Taihe 9 visiting Huihu presented seven horse-archery women from Princess Taihe and two Shatuo boys.

sentences.zh: 開成初，其相有安允合者，與特勒柴草欲篡薩特勒可汗，薩特勒可汗覺，殺柴草及安允合。

translations.literal: At the start of Kaicheng, among their chancellors was Anyunhe, who with teli Chaicao wished to usurp Qaghan Sateler; Sateler perceived it and killed Chaicao and Anyunhe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaicheng chancellor Anyunhe and teli Chaicao plotted against Qaghan Sateler; Sateler discovered and executed them.

sentences.zh: 又有回鶻相掘羅勿者，擁兵在外，怨誅柴草、安允合，又殺薩特勒可汗，以馺特勒為可汗。

translations.literal: There was also Huihu chancellor Jueluowu, holding troops outside, resenting the execution of Chaicao and Anyunhe; he again killed Qaghan Sateler and installed Wusa Teli as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Jueluowu, commanding troops abroad, resented those killings, slew Sateler, and raised Wusa Teli as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 有將軍句錄末賀恨掘羅勿，走引黠戛斯領十萬騎破回鶻城，殺馺，斬掘羅勿，燒蕩殆盡，回鶻散奔諸蕃。

translations.literal: General Juluomohe hated Jueluowu, fled and led the Kirghiz with one hundred thousand horsemen to break the Huihu city, killed Wusa, beheaded Jueluowu, burned and ravaged nearly all, and the Huihu scattered fleeing to various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: General Juluomohe, hating Jueluowu, fled and brought Kirghiz with one hundred thousand riders to smash the Huihu capital, killed Wusa, slew Jueluowu, burned the city, and sent Huihu fleeing to every quarter.

sentences.zh: 有回鶻相馺職者，擁外甥龐特勒及男鹿並遏粉等兄弟五人、一十五部西奔葛邏祿，一支投吐蕃，一支投安西，又有近可汗牙十三部，以特勒烏介為可汗，南來附漢。

translations.literal: There was Huihu chancellor Sazhi, holding his sister's son Teli Pangteli and Nanlu together with Efen and other five brothers of fifteen divisions fleeing west to the Karluks; one branch submitted to Tibet, one to Anxi; another thirteen divisions near the royal tent made Teli Wujie qaghan and came south to attach to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Sazhi fled west with Teli Pangteli, Nanlu, Efen, five brothers, and fifteen divisions toward the Karluks; one branch went to Tibet, one to Anxi; thirteen divisions near the old camp made Teli Wujie qaghan and came south to Tang.

sentences.zh: 初，黠戛斯破回鶻，得太和公主。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Kirghiz broke the Huihu they captured Princess Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kirghiz shattered the Huihu they took Princess Taihe.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯自稱李陵之後，與國同姓，遂令達幹十人送公主至塞上。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz claimed descent from Li Ling and the same surname as the state; they ordered ten dagan to escort the princess to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming descent from Li Ling and kinship with Tang, the Kirghiz sent ten dagan to escort her to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 烏介途遇黠戛斯使，達幹等並被殺。

translations.literal: Wujie encountered the Kirghiz envoys on the road; the dagan were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie met the Kirghiz escort on the road and killed the dagan.

sentences.zh: 太和公主卻歸烏介可汗，乃質公主同行，南渡大磧。

translations.literal: Princess Taihe returned to Qaghan Wujie, who then held her as hostage to travel together, crossing the great desert southward.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe returned to Wujie, who kept her as hostage and crossed the great desert south with her.

sentences.zh: 至天德界，奏請天德城與太和公主居。

translations.literal: Reaching Tiande territory, they memorialized asking to dwell at Tiande city with Princess Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Tiande, they asked to lodge at Tiande city with Princess Taihe.

sentences.zh: 有回鶻相赤心者，與連位相姓仆固者，與特勤那頡啜擁部眾，不賓烏介。

translations.literal: There was Huihu chancellor Chixin and consecutive chancellor surnamed Pugu, with teli Nanechuo holding tribes, not submitting to Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chixin and chancellor Pugu with teli Nanechuo held tribes loyal not to Wujie.

sentences.zh: 赤心欲犯塞，烏介遣其屬霡沒斯先布誠於天德軍使田牟，然後誘赤心宰相同謁烏介可汗，戮赤心於可汗帳下並仆固二人。

translations.literal: Chixin wished to raid the border; Wujie sent his follower Meimosi first to show good faith to Tiande army commissioner Tian Mou, then lured Chixin and chancellors to audience with Qaghan Wujie and executed Chixin in the qaghan's tent together with the two Pugu men.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin planned a border raid; Wujie sent Meimosi to pledge good faith to Tian Mou at Tiande, then lured Chixin and chancellors to Wujie's tent and killed Chixin and two Pugu men.

sentences.zh: 那頡戰勝，全占赤心下七千帳，東瞰振武、大同，據室韋、黑沙、榆林，東南入幽州雄武軍西北界。

translations.literal: Nanechuo won the fight, wholly taking Chixin's seven thousand tents, looking east toward Zhenwu and Datong, holding Shiwei, Heisha, and Yulin, entering southeast toward the northwest border of Youzhou Xiongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Nanechuo seized all seven thousand tents of Chixin, eyed Zhenwu and Datong, held Shiwei, Heisha, and Yulin, and pressed the northwest marches of Youzhou's Xiongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度使張仲武遣弟仲至率兵大破那頡之眾，全收七千帳，殺戮收擒老小近九萬人。

translations.literal: Youzhou governor Zhang Zhongwu sent his younger brother Zhongzhi with troops and greatly broke Nanechuo's masses, wholly taking the seven thousand tents, killing, capturing, old and young, nearly ninety thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou governor Zhang Zhongwu sent brother Zhongzhi, routed Nanechuo, retook seven thousand tents, and killed or captured nearly ninety thousand.

sentences.zh: 那頡中箭，透駝群潛脫，烏介獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Nanechuo was shot by an arrow, pierced a camel herd and slipped away secretly; Wujie captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanechuo, arrow-struck, hid among camels and escaped; Wujie caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 烏介諸部猶稱十萬眾，駐牙大同軍北閭門山，時會昌二年秋，頻劫東陜已北，天德、振武、雲朔，比罹俘戮。

translations.literal: Wujie's divisions still claimed one hundred thousand; they encamped at Datong Army's northern Lümen Mountain—in the autumn of Huichang year 2 they repeatedly raided east of Shaanxi northward, Tiande, Zhenwu, Yunshuo, all suffering capture and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie still claimed one hundred thousand warriors, camped north of Datong at Lümen Mountain; in autumn Huichang 2 they raided east Shaanxi, Tiande, Zhenwu, and Yunshuo.

sentences.zh: 詔諸道兵悉至防捍，以河東節度使劉沔充南面招控回鶻使；

translations.literal: Edicts ordered troops of all circuits to defend; Hedong governor Liu Yan was made southern commissioner to control Huihu;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts massed frontier troops; Hedong governor Liu Yan became southern commissioner against the Huihu;

sentences.zh: 以幽州節度使張仲武充東面招控回鶻使。

translations.literal: Youzhou governor Zhang Zhongwu was made eastern commissioner to control Huihu.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou governor Zhang Zhongwu became eastern commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，三年春，回鶻特勒龐俱遮、阿敦寧二部，回鶻公主密羯可敦一部，外相諸洛固阿跌一部，及牙帳大將曹磨你等七部，共三萬眾，相次降於幽州，詔配諸道。

translations.literal: Winter of year 2 and spring of year 3—Huihu teli Pangjuzhe, Adingning two divisions, Huihu princess Mijie khatun one division, outer chancellor Zhuoluogu Adie one division, and royal tent great general Caomonini and seven other divisions, thirty thousand in all, successively surrendered at Youzhou and were assigned to various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Huichang 2 through spring 3, teli Pangjuzhe, Adingning, Princess Mijie khatun's division, outer chancellor Zhuoluogu Adie, great general Caomonini, and seven divisions—thirty thousand total—surrendered at Youzhou and were distributed.

sentences.zh: 有特勒霡沒斯、阿歷支、習勿啜三部，回鶻相愛耶勿弘順、回鶻尚書呂衡等諸部降振武，三部首領皆賜姓李氏，及名思忠、思貞、思惠、思恩，充歸義使。

translations.literal: Teli Meimosi, Alizhi, Xiwuchuo three divisions, chancellor Aiyewu Hongshun, Huihu secretary Lu Heng and other divisions surrendered at Zhenwu; the three division chieftains were all granted surname Li and names Sizhong, Sizhen, Sihui, Sien, as Guiyi commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Meimosi, Alizhi, Xiwuchuo, chancellor Hongshun, secretary Lu Heng, and others surrendered at Zhenwu; three chiefs received the Li surname and names Sizhong, Sizhen, Sihui, Sien as commissioners of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 有特勒葉被沽兄李二部南奔吐蕃，有特勒可質力二部東北奔大室韋，有特勒荷勿啜東討契丹，戰死。

translations.literal: Teli Yebegu brother Li two divisions fled south to Tibet; teli Kezhili two divisions fled northeast to great Shiwei; teli Hewuchuo marched east against the Khitan and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Teli Yebegu brother Li's two divisions fled to Tibet; Kezhili's two divisions fled to great Shiwei; Hewuchuo attacked the Khitan eastward and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年，回鶻尚書仆固繹到幽州，約以太和公主歸幽州，烏介去幽州界八十里下營。

translations.literal: In Huichang year 3, Huihu secretary Pugu Yi reached Youzhou, arranging for Princess Taihe to return to Youzhou; Wujie camped eighty li from Youzhou's border.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 3 secretary Pugu Yi reached Youzhou to arrange Princess Taihe's return; Wujie camped eighty li from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 其親信骨肉及摩尼誌凈等四人已先入振武軍。

translations.literal: His trusted kin and Manichaean Zhijing and four others had already entered Zhenwu Army first.
translations.idiomatic: His kin and Manichaean Zhijing plus four others had already entered Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 是夜，河東劉沔率兵奄至烏介營，烏介驚走東北約四百里外，依和解室韋下營，不及將太和公主同走。

translations.literal: That night Hedong Liu Yan led troops suddenly upon Wujie's camp; Wujie fled in alarm northeast about four hundred li, relying on the reconciled Shiwei to camp, unable to take Princess Taihe along.
translations.idiomatic: That night Liu Yan stormed Wujie's camp; Wujie fled four hundred li northeast to Shiwei allies without Taihe.

sentences.zh: 豐州刺史石雄兵遇太和公主帳，因迎歸國。

translations.literal: Fengzhou governor Shi Xiong's troops met Princess Taihe's tent and escorted her home.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhou governor Shi Xiong met Taihe's camp and brought her home.

sentences.zh: 烏介部眾至大中元年詣幽州降，留者漂流餓凍，眾十萬，所存止三千已下。

translations.literal: Wujie's tribes surrendered at Youzhou in the first year of Dazhong; those remaining drifted, starving and freezing—of one hundred thousand, barely three thousand or fewer survived.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie's people surrendered at Youzhou in Dazhong 1; survivors of the hundred thousand numbered barely three thousand.

sentences.zh: 烏介嫁妹與室韋，托附之。

translations.literal: Wujie married his younger sister to the Shiwei and relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie married his sister into the Shiwei and clung to them.

sentences.zh: 為回鶻相美權者逸隱啜逼諸回鶻殺烏介於金山，以其弟特勒遏撚為可汗，復有眾五千以上，其食用糧羊皆取給於奚王碩舍朗。

translations.literal: Huihu chancellor Meiquanzhe Yiyinchuo forced the Huihu to kill Wujie at Jinshan, installing his younger brother Teli Enian as qaghan; again they had more than five thousand; food, grain, and sheep all came from Xi king Shuoshelang.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Meiquanzhe Yiyinchuo forced Huihu to kill Wujie at Jinshan and made brother Teli Enian qaghan; five thousand remained, fed by Xi king Shuoshelang.

sentences.zh: 大中元年春，張仲武大破奚眾，其回鶻無所取給，日有耗散。

translations.literal: In spring of Dazhong year 1, Zhang Zhongwu greatly defeated Xi forces; the Huihu had no supplies and daily dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: In spring Dazhong 1 Zhang Zhongwu crushed the Xi; the Huihu, bereft of supplies, melted away daily.

sentences.zh: 至二年春，唯存名王貴臣五百人已下，依室韋。

translations.literal: By spring of year 2 only five hundred or fewer noble ministers remained, relying on the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: By spring Dazhong 2 barely five hundred nobles remained with the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 張鐘武因賀正室韋經過幽州，仲武卻令還蕃，遣送遏撚等來向幽州，遏撚等懼，是夜與妻葛祿、子特勒毒斯等九騎西走，余眾奔之不及，回鶻諸相達官老幼大哭。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu, as Shiwei passed Youzhou for New Year's audience, sent them back; Enian and others were sent toward Youzhou; Enian and company feared— that night with wife Karluk, son Teli Dusi, and nine riders fled west; the rest could not follow and all Huihu chancellors and officials, old and young, wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu sent Shiwei home from Youzhou's New Year rites; Enian was marched toward Youzhou but fled west that night with wife, son Dusi, and nine riders; left behind, Huihu officials wept.

sentences.zh: 室韋分回鶻余眾為七分，七姓室韋各占一分。

translations.literal: The Shiwei divided the remaining Huihu into seven parts; seven Shiwei clans each took one share.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwei split the remnant Huihu seven ways among seven clans.

sentences.zh: 經三宿，黠戛斯相阿播領諸蕃兵稱七萬，從西南天德北界來取遏撚及諸回鶻，大敗室韋。

translations.literal: After three nights Kirghiz chancellor A'bo led various tribal troops claiming seventy thousand from the southwest Tiande northern border to seize Enian and the Huihu and greatly defeated the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: After three nights Kirghiz chancellor A'bo led seventy thousand from southwest of Tiande to seize Enian and crushed the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 回鶻在室韋者，阿播皆收歸磧北。

translations.literal: Huihu among the Shiwei were all taken back north of the desert by A'bo.
translations.idiomatic: Huihu left with the Shiwei were all reclaimed north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 在外猶數帳，散藏諸山深林，盜劫諸蕃，皆西向傾心望安西龐勒之到。

translations.literal: Still several tents remained outside, hiding in deep mountains and forests, robbing various tribes—all looked west hoping for Anxi's Pangle to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered tents hid in forests, raiding tribes—all looked west for Anxi's Pangle.

sentences.zh: 龐勒已自稱可汗，有磧西諸城。

translations.literal: Pangle had already styled himself qaghan, holding cities of the western desert.
translations.idiomatic: Pangle already called himself qaghan, holding western desert cities.

sentences.zh: 其後嗣君弱臣強，居甘州，無復昔時之盛。

translations.literal: Later successors were weak rulers with strong ministers, dwelling at Ganzhou, no longer possessing former splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers grew weak while ministers grew strong, seated at Ganzhou without former glory.

sentences.zh: 到今時遣使入朝，進玉馬二物及本土所產，交易而返。

translations.literal: To the present they still send envoys to court, presenting two jade horses and local products, trading and returning.
translations.idiomatic: To this day they still send envoys with jade horses and local goods, trade, and return.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自三代以前，兩漢之後，西羌、北狄，互興部族，其名不同，為患一也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Before the Three Dynasties, after the Two Han, western Qiang and northern Di repeatedly rose in tribal confederations—their names differed, the harm was one.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From antiquity through Han, western Qiang and northern Di rose under many names yet brought the same harm.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕云：「邊陲之患，為手足之疥；

translations.literal: Cai Yong said: "Border troubles are like scabs on hands and feet;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong wrote: "Frontier trouble is a rash upon the limbs;

sentences.zh: 中國之困，為胸背之疽。

translations.literal: China's distress is like a carbuncle on chest and back."
translations.idiomatic: the empire's affliction is a boil upon the vitals."

sentences.zh: 突厥為煬帝之患深矣，隋竟滅；

translations.literal: The Turks deeply harmed Emperor Yang of Sui, and Sui in the end perished;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks ravaged Sui Yangdi's reign and Sui at last fell;

sentences.zh: 中國之困，其理昭然。

translations.literal: China's distress—the principle is clear.
translations.idiomatic: the empire's peril—the lesson is plain.

sentences.zh: 」自太宗平突厥，破延陀，而回紇興焉。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Taizong pacified the Turks and broke the Yantuo, the Huihe rose.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong subdued the Turks and shattered the Yantuo, the Huihe came to prominence.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸靈武以降之，置州府以安之，以名爵玉帛以恩之。

translations.literal: Taizong went in person to Lingwu to receive their surrender, established prefectures and districts to settle them, and used titles, seals, and silks to show grace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong himself went to Lingwu to accept their submission, set up prefectures to settle them, and honored them with ranks, seals, and silks.

sentences.zh: 其義何哉？

translations.literal: What was the meaning of this?
translations.idiomatic: What was the reasoning behind this?

sentences.zh: 蓋以狄不可盡，而以威惠羈縻之。

translations.literal: It was because the Di could not be exhausted, and so they were bridled with majesty and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Simply put, the northern peoples could not be destroyed outright; they had to be harnessed through power and kindness.

sentences.zh: 開元中，三綱正，百姓足，四夷八蠻，翕然向化，要荒之外，畏威懷惠，不其盛矣！

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era the three bonds were upright, the common people were sufficient, and the four quarters and eight barbarians all turned toward civilization; beyond the frontier they feared majesty and cherished kindness—is this not splendor!
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan the moral order stood firm and the people were content; far tribes turned toward civilization, and beyond the marches they feared Tang might yet welcomed its grace—was that not greatness!

sentences.zh: 天寶末，奸臣弄權於內，逆臣跋扈於外，內外結釁而車駕遽遷，華夷生心而神器將墜。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao wicked ministers manipulated power within and rebellious ministers swaggered without; inner and outer joined in strife and the imperial carriage hurried away; Chinese and barbarians alike took heart while the sacred vessel nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: By late Tianbao corrupt ministers held sway at court and rebel warlords abroad; court and frontier collided, the emperor fled, hearts divided across the empire, and the throne itself trembled.

sentences.zh: 肅宗誘回紇以復京畿。

translations.literal: Suzong enticed the Huihe to recover the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong enlisted the Huihe to retake the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗誘回紇以平河朔。

translations.literal: Daizong enticed the Huihe to pacify Heshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong enlisted the Huihe to pacify the Hebei region.

sentences.zh: 戡難中興之功，大即大矣！

translations.literal: Merit in quelling disaster and restoring the dynasty—great indeed, great!
translations.idiomatic: Their service in saving the dynasty from ruin was immense—immense indeed!

sentences.zh: 然生靈之膏血已幹，不能供其求取；

translations.literal: Yet the people's lifeblood was already drained dry and could not supply their demands;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people's substance was already drained and could not satisfy their demands;

sentences.zh: 朝廷之法令並弛，無以抑其憑陵。

translations.literal: court laws and orders all slackened and could not restrain their bullying.
translations.idiomatic: imperial law had grown lax and could not curb their arrogance.

sentences.zh: 忍恥和親，姑息不暇。

translations.literal: Bearing humiliation through marriage alliances, indulgence left no respite.
translations.idiomatic: The court swallowed humiliation in marriage alliances; indulgence knew no pause.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩為叛，尤甚阽危；

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, peril was extreme;
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en's rebellion brought the gravest danger;

sentences.zh: 郭子儀之能軍，終免侵軼。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi's ability to command armies finally averted invasion.
translations.idiomatic: only Guo Ziyi's generalship at last kept invasion at bay.

sentences.zh: 比昔諸戎，於國之功最大，為民之害亦深。

translations.literal: Compared with past foreign tribes, their service to the state was greatest and their harm to the people deepest.
translations.idiomatic: Among all frontier peoples, they aided the state most—and harmed the people most.

sentences.zh: 及勢利日隆，盛衰時變，冰消瓦解，如存若亡，竟為手足之疥焉。

translations.literal: As power and profit daily waxed and fortune and decline shifted with the times, they melted like ice and shattered like tiles, as if existing yet not existing, and in the end became but a scab on hand and foot.
translations.idiomatic: As their power swelled and fortunes turned, they dissolved like ice, broke like tile, seeming to exist yet not—until at last they were no more than a rash upon the limbs.

sentences.zh: 僖、昭之世，黃、硃叠興，竟為胸背之疽焉。

translations.literal: In the Xizong and Zhaozong eras Huang Chao and Zhu Wen rose in turn and became the carbuncle on chest and back.
translations.idiomatic: Under emperors Xizong and Zhaozong, Huang Chao and Zhu Wen arose in turn—the true carbuncle on chest and back.

sentences.zh: 手疥背疽，誠為確論。

translations.literal: Scab on the hand, carbuncle on the back—the theory is sound indeed.
translations.idiomatic: A rash on the limbs, a boil on the vitals—the analogy holds.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：土德初隆，比屋可封。

translations.literal: In praise: When the virtue of earth first flourished, every household could be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Praise runs: When earthly virtue first ascended, every hearth seemed worthy of honor.

sentences.zh: 朝綱中否，邊鄙興戎。

translations.literal: When court discipline faltered, borderlands raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: When the court's order failed, the marches took up arms.

sentences.zh: 安、史亂國，回紇恃功。

translations.literal: An Lushan and Shi Siming threw the state into chaos; the Huihe relied on their merit.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan and Shi Siming wrecked the realm; the Huihe traded on their service.

sentences.zh: 恃功伊何？

translations.literal: Relying on merit—how so?
translations.idiomatic: What did that reliance mean?

sentences.zh: 鹹議姑息。

translations.literal: All agreed on indulgent forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Every voice counseled appeasement.

sentences.zh: 民不聊生，國殫其力。

translations.literal: The people could not live; the state exhausted its strength.
translations.idiomatic: The people had no peace; the empire spent its last strength.

sentences.zh: 華夷有截，盛衰如織。

translations.literal: Chinese and barbarian realms were divided; rise and fall wove like cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Han and tribal worlds stood apart; glory and ruin interwove like threads.

sentences.zh: 彼既長惡，我乃修德，疽疥之義，百代可則。

translations.literal: When they long indulged evil, we cultivated virtue—the meaning of carbuncle and scab may guide a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: They persisted in wrong; we turned to virtue—the lesson of boil and rash may instruct a hundred generations.
